definition_zh: v. 有益于；起作用；（用于反身句式）利用；n. 效用；益处（多见于固定短语）
definition_en: To be of use or help; reflexively, to make use of an offer or chance; as a noun, use or benefit, now mainly in set phrases.
core_image: 手里那点力气到底顶不顶用
scene: 律师劝他利用这次免费复核的机会。 The lawyer urged him to avail himself of the free review.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：avail oneself of 表示利用某个机会或条件，是这个词最常见的现代用法。

senses.title: To be of use
senses.definition: to help or produce a useful effect, often used in the negative
senses.definitionCN: 有所帮助或产生有用的效果，常用于否定句
senses.example: Protests availed nothing against the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议对该决定毫无作用。
senses.why: Avail joins a-, to, with val, worth, so it literally means to be worth something to someone.
senses.whyCN: avail 由 a-「向」与 val「价值」构成，字面就是「对某人有价值」。

senses.title: To make use of
senses.definition: in the reflexive pattern avail oneself of, to take advantage of an offer, chance or facility
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身句式，指利用某个机会、条件或设施
senses.example: Few residents availed themselves of the grant.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有居民利用这项补助。
senses.why: If something is worth something to you, you can turn that worth to account, which is exactly what the reflexive pattern says.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物对你有价值，你就可以把这份价值用起来，这正是反身句式所表达的意思。

senses.title: Use or benefit
senses.definition: as a noun, help or advantage, surviving chiefly in set phrases of little use
senses.definitionCN: 作名词指帮助或好处，主要保留在表示收效甚微的固定短语中
senses.example: All their pleading was of no avail.
senses.exampleCN: 他们所有的恳求都毫无用处。
senses.why: The noun kept the old sense of worth, and because it froze inside set phrases it now sounds formal.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「价值」这一旧义，又因固定在短语内部，如今听起来偏正式。

intro.en: Avail is a- plus vail, from Old French valoir, to be worth, from Latin valere, to be strong or worth; the same root gives value and valid.
intro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail，出自古法语 valoir「有价值」，源自拉丁语 valere「强健、有价值」；同一词根产生 value 与 valid。

items.en: A root meaning to be strong lies behind words of worth, health and power.
items.cn: 一个表示「强健」的词根支撑着价值、健康与力量类的词。

items.en: Latin valere meant to be strong, to be well, and hence to be worth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为「强健、安好」，进而指「有价值」。

items.en: Old French valoir kept the sense of being worth a price or a benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 保留了「值某个价钱或有某种好处」的意思。

items.en: With a-, to, added, avaloir meant to be of profit to someone.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 avaloir，意为「对某人有益」。

items.en: Middle English availen meant to help or profit, both as verb and noun.
items.cn: 中古英语 availen 意为「有益、有帮助」，动词名词皆可。

items.en: The bare verb faded, leaving the reflexive pattern and phrases meaning in vain.
items.cn: 单独的动词用法衰退，留下反身句式与表示徒劳的短语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the val family and two words of similar sound; the near-meaning group lists plainer words for being of use.
note.cn: 形近组保留 val 词族和两个读音相近的词；近义组列出表示「有用」的更平易的词。

entries.definition: Ready to be used or got.
To prove stronger, to win through.
A covering for the face.
To cry out in grief.
To make things easier for someone.
To do good to, or the good done.
To employ for a purpose.
To gain advantage from.

normalIntro.en: Avail is a- plus vail, a cousin of value: to be worth something to you, or to turn that worth to use.
normalIntro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail，与 value 同族：对你有价值，或把这份价值用起来。

normal.en: The live pattern is avail oneself of.
normal.cn: 仍在使用的句式是反身加 of 的结构。

normal.en: To no avail means the effort failed.
normal.cn: 表示徒劳的短语说明努力白费。

normal.en: Of little avail means almost useless.
normal.cn: 表示收效甚微的短语意为几乎无用。

normal.en: The root val also gives value and valid.
normal.cn: 词根 val 也产生 value 与 valid。

normal.en: Avail is formal; use is everyday.
normal.cn: avail 偏正式，use 是日常用词。

abstract.en: Picture strength that finally moves a weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一股终于推动重物的力气。

abstract.en: Imagine an open door you decide to walk through.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇敞开的门，你决定走进去。

abstract.en: Think of shouting into wind that ignores you.
abstract.cn: 想象对着不理你的风喊话。

examples.en: She availed herself of the shuttle bus.
examples.cn: 她利用了那趟班车。

examples.en: Their warnings availed little.
examples.cn: 他们的警告收效甚微。

examples.en: He argued for an hour, to no avail.
examples.cn: 他争了一小时，徒劳无功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ vail（与 value 同族，「价值」）——对你有价值就是 avail「有用」，把这份价值用起来就是「利用」。

root: 拉丁语 valere「强健、有价值」经古法语 valoir 加 a-「向」成 avaloir「对……有益」，入中古英语作 availen；现代主要保留反身句式与表示徒劳的固定短语。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses turn on worth: something being worth something to you, your turning that worth to use, and the worth itself named as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都围绕「价值」：某物对你有价值、你把这份价值用起来，以及把这份价值本身当名词来称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: whether the strength in your hand actually counts for anything
core.cn: 核心意象：手里那点力气到底顶不顶用

branches.en: Warnings that changed nothing.
branches.cn: 毫无作用的警告。

branches.en: Protests that failed against a decision.
branches.cn: 对决定无效的抗议。

branches.en: A resident taking up a grant.
branches.cn: 申领补助的居民。

branches.en: Pleading that was of no use.
branches.cn: 毫无用处的恳求。

branches.en: Both measure how much the effort was worth.
branches.cn: 两者都在衡量这份努力值多少。

intro.en: Avail is a- plus vail; the val root builds value, valid, prevail and equivalent.
intro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail；val 词根构成 value、valid、prevail 与 equivalent。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is valere, to be strong, and valor, worth; the -able ending turns it into available.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 valere「强健」与 valor「价值」；加上 -able 词尾便成 available。

definition_zh: 恶化；加剧；激怒
definition_en: the act of making a bad condition, problem, or feeling worse or more intense
core_image: 一滴苦汁搅进清水，越搅越苦、越难下咽
scene: 医生翻看病历，发现病人昨夜喘得比前一天更厉害。 The nurse noted an exacerbation of asthma after the cold snap.
sceneCN: 这里 exacerbation 是「加重、恶化」（第 1 个义项：病情突然加重）；句意：护士注意到寒潮过后病人的哮喘加重了。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀 -ation 还原的动词，义为「使恶化；加剧；激怒」
动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「使情况恶化的；令人恼火的」
过去分词转作的形容词，义为「被加重的；被激怒的」

senses.title: A worsening of a disease
senses.definition: a sudden increase in the severity of a disease or of its symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或其症状严重程度的突然上升
senses.example: The patient was admitted with an acute exacerbation of asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因哮喘急性加重而入院。
senses.why: Latin acerbus means bitter and harsh, and exacerbare means to make a thing more bitter, so the noun first names a disease turning harsher.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acerbus 意为苦涩、猛烈，exacerbare 就是把东西弄得更苦，所以这个名词最先指病情转向更凶的那一刻。

senses.title: An increase in the severity of a problem
senses.definition: the act of making a problem, a conflict, or a bad situation worse
senses.definitionCN: 使问题、冲突或糟糕局面变得更严重的行为或过程
senses.example: Poverty is both a result and an exacerbation of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困既是危机的结果，也是危机的加剧因素。
senses.why: The medical image spread outward: any condition that can be made bitter can be made worse, so the noun came to name the sharpening of social and political troubles.
senses.whyCN: 医学意象向外扩散：凡是可以变「苦」的状况都可以被弄得更糟，于是这个名词也指社会与政治困境的加剧。

senses.title: The act of irritating or provoking
senses.definition: the act of making a person angry or irritated
senses.definitionCN: 使某人生气或恼怒的行为
senses.example: His calm questions were an exacerbation rather than a comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的追问与其说是安慰，不如说是激怒。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to provoke, because bitterness was felt as a sting, and the noun kept that older sense of pricking someone into anger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词还含「挑动」义，因为苦涩被感受为一种刺；名词保留了更早的「刺人发怒」这一层。

senses.title: A countable flare-up episode
senses.definition: a distinct episode in which symptoms flare up and then settle again
senses.definitionCN: 症状突然发作、随后又平复的一次独立病程
senses.example: She recorded three exacerbations in the past year.
senses.exampleCN: 她记录下去年有三次急性加重。
senses.why: Doctors needed to count these events, so the noun moved from an abstract worsening to a single attack, and the plural marks one episode at a time.
senses.whyCN: 医生需要清点这类事件，名词便从抽象的「恶化」转为一次具体的发作，复数正指一次一次单独的发作。

intro.en: Exacerbation comes from Latin acerbus, bitter or harsh, through the verb exacerbare, to make worse or to provoke.
intro.cn: exacerbation 源自拉丁语 acerbus（苦涩、猛烈），经由动词 exacerbare（使恶化、激怒）而来。

items.en: Acerbus means harsh, bitter, or sour, and its sharper cousin acer means keen or cutting.
items.cn: acerbus 意为猛烈、苦涩、酸；它更尖利的近亲 acer 意为锐利、锋利的。

items.en: The verb exacerbare joins ex- to acerbus and means to make harsh, to aggravate, or to provoke.
items.cn: 动词 exacerbare 由 ex- 与 acerbus 合成，意为使变苦、加重或激怒。

items.en: The action noun exacerbatio names the making worse of a condition or of a temper.
items.cn: 动作名词 exacerbatio 指病情或情绪的加重。

items.en: Medical writing in French carries exacerbation forward as a term for a graver turn of illness.
items.cn: 法语医学文献把 exacerbation 传下去，用作病情转向更重的术语。

items.en: English takes the word as a learned medical noun for the sharpening of a disease.
items.cn: 英语接受了这个词，把它当作表示病情加重的学术医学名词。

items.en: Modern usage widens it to problems, conflicts, and countable attacks of illness.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到问题、冲突，以及可数的病情发作。

note.en: Exacerbation sits in the bitter family of acerbus, beside the verb exacerbate, and near the plain worsening words.
note.cn: exacerbation 属于 acerbus 的「苦涩」词族，与动词 exacerbate 同根，也与平实的「恶化」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a bad situation or feeling worse
entries.definitionCN: 使糟糕的局面或情绪变得更糟

entries.definition: bitter or sharp in tone
entries.definitionCN: 言辞尖酸刻薄的；同出「苦涩」词根

entries.definition: a feeling of intense irritation
entries.definitionCN: 极度恼火——与 exacerbation 只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 asper「粗糙」）

entries.definition: the act of making something worse
the process of becoming worse in quality or condition
entries.definitionCN: 质量或状况变坏的过程

entries.definition: a sudden burst of a disease or of anger
entries.definitionCN: 疾病的突然发作；怒气的突然爆发

normalIntro.en: Exacerbation keeps the Latin taste of bitterness: whatever is exacerbated has been made harsher.
normalIntro.cn: exacerbation 保留着拉丁语「苦涩」的味道：被加剧的东西都变得更凶了。

normal.en: Acute exacerbation is a fixed medical phrase for a sudden flare-up.
normal.cn: acute exacerbation 是固定医学说法，指突然的急性加重。

normal.en: Exacerbate is the verb, while exasperate is a different word with a different root.
normal.cn: exacerbate 是动词，exasperate 则是另一个词，词根并不相同。

normal.en: The prefix ex- pushes the meaning outward, so the condition breaks out worse.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 把意义向外推，于是病情「爆」得更凶。

normal.en: Planners speak of exacerbating traffic problems, meaning the jams get worse.
normal.cn: 规划者会说「加剧交通问题」，意思就是堵得更厉害。

normal.en: Hospitals count exacerbations, so the plural is common in case reports.
normal.cn: 医院会统计发作次数，所以复数形式在病例报告中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture one bitter drop stirred into clear water until every sip turns harsh.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴苦汁搅进清水，每一口都变得更苦。

abstract.en: Imagine a hairline crack in a dam widening as the water presses on it.
abstract.cn: 想象堤坝上一道细缝在水压下越裂越宽。

abstract.en: Feel a splinter under the skin: the more you touch it, the angrier the spot grows.
abstract.cn: 想象皮肤下扎了一根刺，越碰那处越发红发火。

examples.en: The heat wave brought an exacerbation of her breathing problems.
examples.cn: 热浪使她的呼吸问题加重了。

examples.en: Poverty is both a result and an exacerbation of the crisis.
examples.cn: 贫困既是危机的结果，也是危机的加剧因素。

examples.en: Doctors counted four exacerbations during the winter.
examples.cn: 医生统计出冬季有四次急性加重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挨个撒盐」——读起来像挨个往伤口撒盐，越撒越疼，就是「恶化、激怒」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、加强）+ acerbus（苦涩、猛烈）→ 动词 exacerbare（使更苦、激怒）→ 名词 exacerbatio → 英语 exacerbation，核心义「把状况弄得更苦更凶」。

sensesIntro.en: Exacerbation starts as the medical worsening of a disease, widens to any problem made worse, keeps the older sense of provocation, and ends as a countable flare-up.
sensesIntro.cn: exacerbation 先是医学上病情的加重，再扩展到任何问题的恶化，又保留更早的「激怒」义，最后成为可数的一次发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bitter drop stirred into clear water until it turns harsh.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴苦汁搅进清水，直到整杯变苦。

branches.en: A disease turning worse is the medical core of the word.
branches.cn: 病情转为更重，是这个词的医学核心义。

branches.en: Any bad situation can be made harsher, which is the widened sense.
branches.cn: 任何糟糕局面都能被弄得更凶，这是扩展后的义项。

branches.en: The old sense of pricking someone into anger survives beside it.
branches.cn: 「刺人发怒」的旧义一直与它并存。

branches.en: A countable attack is one concrete turn for the worse.
branches.cn: 可数的一次发作，就是一次具体的恶化。

branches.en: A worsened problem and a provoked person are both things made bitter.
branches.cn: 被加剧的问题与被激怒的人，都是被弄「苦」了的对象。

intro.en: Exacerbation is built from the Latin prefix ex-, the root acerbus, bitter, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: exacerbation 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、词根 acerbus（苦涩）与名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin acerbus means harsh or bitter, and exacerbare means to make harsh or to provoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acerbus 意为苦涩、猛烈，exacerbare 意为使变苦、激怒。

items.example: The prefix ex- intensifies the bitterness.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 加强了「苦」的程度。

items.example: Acerbus describes a sharp and bitter taste.
items.exampleCN: acerbus 描述尖锐苦涩的味道。

items.example: Acer is the sharper cousin of acerbus.
items.exampleCN: acer 是 acerbus 更尖利的近亲。
exacerbare 由 ex- 与 acerbus 合成。

items.example: Exacerbatio is the Latin action noun.
items.exampleCN: exacerbatio 是拉丁语的动作名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation builds a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Do not confuse it with exasperate.
items.exampleCN: 注意不要把它与 exasperate 混淆。

items.example: Exacerbating factors keep the disease active.
items.exampleCN: 加重因素让疾病持续活动。

items.example: Exasperate comes from asper, rough, not from acerbus.
items.exampleCN: exasperate 来自 asper（粗糙），并非来自 acerbus。

items.example: Acerbic wit shares the bitter root.
items.exampleCN: acerbic 的尖刻共享「苦」这个词根。

definition_zh: n. 弧，弧线；电弧；（故事或人生的）发展轨迹　v. 呈弧形移动；形成电弧
definition_en: A curved line or path, like part of a circle; a bright electric discharge across a gap; the shape of a story or career as it rises and falls; as a verb, to move in a curve.
core_image: 弯过来的一段线，从这头连到那头
scene: 球在空中划出一道长长的弧线。 The ball traced a long arc across the sky.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arc 指弯曲的一段线或路径，形状像圆的一部分。

senses.title: A curved line or path
senses.definition: a part of a circle or other curve, or the curved path a moving object follows
senses.definitionCN: 圆或其他曲线的一段，或运动物体所走的弯曲路径
senses.example: The lamp threw an arc of light on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 灯在墙上投出一道弧形的光。
senses.why: Latin arcus meant a bow, and a bent bow is exactly this shape, so every sense keeps that single bend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，拉开的弓正是这个形状，所以各个义项都保留着那一道弯。

senses.title: A bright electric discharge
senses.definition: a luminous bridge of current jumping across a gap between two electrodes, used in welding and old lamps
senses.definitionCN: 电流跨过两个电极间隙形成的发光桥，用于焊接与早期灯具
senses.example: An arc jumped between the two worn contacts.
senses.exampleCN: 两个磨损的触点之间跳起了电弧。
senses.why: The discharge bends like a bow between the terminals, so the shape word was borrowed for the phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: 放电在两端之间弯成弓形，于是这个表形状的词被借来指这一现象。

senses.title: The shape of a story
senses.definition: the course a narrative, character or career takes as it rises, turns and resolves
senses.definitionCN: 叙事、人物或事业在上升、转折与收束中所走的历程
senses.example: The novel gives every minor character a full arc.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说给每个配角都安排了完整的发展线。
senses.why: Plot drawn on paper looks like a rising and falling curve, so the geometry word became a term for narrative shape.
senses.whyCN: 把情节画在纸上就是一条起落的曲线，于是这个几何词变成了叙事结构的术语。

senses.title: To move in a curve
senses.definition: of a moving thing, to travel along a curved path rather than a straight one
senses.definitionCN: 指运动之物沿弯曲路径而非直线行进
senses.example: The gull arced low over the water and turned back.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥贴着水面划了个弧又折回来。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb with no change of shape: the path becomes the action of following that path.
senses.whyCN: 名词不变形就转为动词：路径本身变成了「走这条路径」的动作。

intro.en: Arc is Latin arcus, a bow or arch, from an ancient root meaning bow. English took it through Old French arc as a geometry term, then extended it to electricity and to stories.
intro.cn: arc 就是拉丁语 arcus「弓、拱」，出自一个意为「弓」的古老词根。英语经古法语 arc 作为几何术语吸收，后来扩展到电学与叙事。

items.en: The reconstructed root arkw- meant bow, the bent weapon that gave the whole family its shape.
items.cn: 重构词根 arkw- 意为「弓」，这件弯曲的武器给整个词族提供了形状。

items.en: Latin arcus meant a bow, and by extension any arch or curve, including the rainbow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，引申指任何拱或曲线，也包括彩虹。

items.en: Old French arc kept both bow and curve, and passed the geometrical sense to English.
items.cn: 古法语 arc 兼指弓与曲线，并把几何义传给英语。

items.en: English recorded arc in the late fourteenth century for a segment of a circle or curve.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末记录 arc，指圆或曲线的一段。

items.en: Humphry Davy demonstrated the electric arc in the early nineteenth century, and the bow-shaped flame kept the name.
items.cn: 戴维在 19 世纪初演示了电弧，那道弓形的火焰沿用了这个名字。

items.en: Twentieth-century film and television criticism made story arc a standard term for a plotted course.
items.cn: 20 世纪影视批评把 story arc 变成指情节历程的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against ark, which sounds identical, and arcane, which has a different root; the near-meaning group lists other words for a bend.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与同音的 ark、以及词根不同的 arcane 混淆；近义组列出其他表示「弯」的词。

entries.definition: A curved structure over an opening.
A large boat, as in Noah's ark.
A row of arches; a games hall.
Known only to a few; mysterious.
entries.definitionCN: 只有少数人知道的；神秘的。

entries.definition: A smoothly bending line.
A bent weapon for arrows.
The curved shape of a new moon.
The path of a flying object.

normalIntro.en: Arc is the bow shape: a bent line, a bent flame, a bent plot, or the act of bending through the air.
normalIntro.cn: arc 就是弓的形状：弯的线、弯的火焰、弯的情节，或在空中弯过去的动作。

normal.en: Arc and arch share the root, but arch is a structure.
normal.cn: arc 与 arch 同根，但 arch 指建筑结构。

normal.en: The verb forms are arced and arcing, with no k.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 arced 与 arcing，不加 k。

normal.en: Story arc is the fixed term in film and fiction.
normal.cn: story arc 是影视与小说的固定术语。

normal.en: Arc sounds like ark, but ark means a boat.
normal.cn: arc 与 ark 同音，但 ark 指船。

normal.en: Arcane looks related but comes from a different root.
normal.cn: arcane 看似相关，其实词根不同。

abstract.en: Picture a drawn bow held still.
abstract.cn: 想象一张拉开后静止的弓。

abstract.en: Imagine a ball writing a curve on the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象球在天上写出一道曲线。

abstract.en: Think of a plot drawn as a hill on paper.
abstract.cn: 想象情节被画成纸上一座小山。

examples.en: The road makes a wide arc around the lake.
examples.cn: 公路绕着湖划出一道大弧。

examples.en: Sparks arced between the loose wires.
examples.cn: 松脱的电线之间迸出弧形火花。

examples.en: Her career follows an unusual arc.
examples.cn: 她的职业生涯走出一条不寻常的轨迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arc 与 arch 同根，拉丁 arcus「弓」——弓弯出来的那段线，就是弧 arc。

root: 原始印欧词根 arkw-「弓」生出拉丁 arcus「弓、拱」，经古法语 arc 进入英语指弧；19 世纪因放电呈弓形而指电弧，20 世纪又借指故事的发展轨迹。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are one bend: a bent line, a bent flame, a bent plot, and the act of moving along a bend.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是同一道弯：弯的线、弯的火焰、弯的情节，以及沿着弯走过去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bent line running from this end to that
core.cn: 核心意象：弯过来的一段线，从这头连到那头

branches.en: A lamp writing light on a wall.
branches.cn: 灯在墙上写出一道光弧。

branches.en: A flame jumping between contacts.
branches.cn: 触点之间跳起的火焰。

branches.en: A plot rising, turning, resolving.
branches.cn: 上升、转折、收束的情节。

branches.en: A gull bending low over water.
branches.cn: 贴着水面弯过去的海鸥。

branches.en: Both are curves you can draw.
branches.cn: 两者都是能画出来的曲线。

intro.en: Arc is the bow root itself, and with -ade and -er it builds arcade and archer; arch is the same root through French.
intro.cn: arc 本身就是「弓」词根，加 -ade 与 -er 构成 arcade 与 archer；arch 是同一词根经法语而来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arcus, a bow, and curvus, bent, which gives curve and curvature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arcus「弓」与 curvus「弯的」，后者产生 curve 与 curvature。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arcus 产生 arc 与 arch。
古法语 arc 传入英语。

definition_zh: n. 杆菌；芽孢杆菌；（大写）芽孢杆菌属
definition_en: A rod-shaped bacterium; with a capital, a genus of such bacteria that form resistant spores.
core_image: 显微镜下一根根短棒似的小东西
scene: 培养皿里那株杆菌一夜之间铺满了培养基。 The bacillus in the dish had covered the medium overnight.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bacillus 泛指呈杆状的细菌，复数为 bacilli。

senses.title: Any rod-shaped bacterium
senses.definition: a bacterium whose cell is shaped like a short rod, whatever its species
senses.definitionCN: 细胞形如短棒的细菌，不论其种类
senses.example: The smear showed a few bacilli.
senses.exampleCN: 涂片显示有少量杆菌。
senses.why: Bacillus is Latin for a little rod, so the name describes the shape seen under the lens, not the disease.
senses.whyCN: bacillus 在拉丁语中意为「小棒」，因此这个名字描述镜下所见的形状，而非疾病。

senses.title: The spore-forming genus
senses.definition: with a capital, a genus of rod-shaped bacteria that form spores able to survive heat and drying
senses.definitionCN: 大写时指一个杆状细菌属，能形成耐热耐干的孢子
senses.example: Bacillus spores survive boiling for minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 芽孢杆菌的孢子能在沸水中存活数分钟。
senses.why: Once microbiology needed exact genera, the shape word was fixed as a formal name for one group.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学需要精确的属名之后，这个形状词就被定为某一群的正式名称。

intro.en: Bacillus is Late Latin bacillus, a little rod, a diminutive of Latin baculus, a stick or staff; the plural bacilli keeps the Latin pattern.
intro.cn: bacillus 是晚期拉丁语 bacillus「小棒」，为拉丁语 baculus「棍、杖」的指小形式；复数 bacilli 保留拉丁语变化。

items.en: A root meaning a staff or support stands behind words for sticks and props.
items.cn: 一个表示「杖、支撑」的词根支撑着棍棒与支柱类的词。

items.en: Latin baculus meant a stick or walking staff, the plain word for a rod.
items.cn: 拉丁语 baculus 意为「棍、手杖」，是指杆的普通词。

items.en: The diminutive bacillus meant a little rod, used for small slender objects.
items.cn: 指小形式 bacillus 意为「小棒」，用于细长的物件。

items.en: Naturalists used bacillus for rod-shaped organisms seen under early microscopes.
items.cn: 博物学者用 bacillus 指早期显微镜下所见的杆状生物。

items.en: Bacteriology fixed Bacillus as a genus of spore-forming rods in the 1870s.
items.cn: 细菌学在 1870 年代把 Bacillus 定为产芽孢杆菌的一个属。

items.en: English kept the Latin plural bacilli, and the word entered public health writing.
items.cn: 英语保留拉丁语复数 bacilli，这个词也进入公共卫生文献。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bacterium family; the near-meaning group lists other shape names used for bacteria.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bacterium 词族；近义组列出用于细菌的其他形状名称。

entries.definition: A single bacterial organism.
Bacterial organisms in general.
Relating to rod-shaped bacteria.
Shaped like a rod.
A spherical bacterium.
A spiral-shaped bacterium.
A microscopic organism.
An organism that causes disease.

normalIntro.en: Bacillus is Latin for a little rod, from baculus, a staff: the name is the shape you see in the lens.
normalIntro.cn: bacillus 在拉丁语中意为「小棒」，出自 baculus「杖」：这个名字就是你在镜头里看到的形状。

normal.en: One bacillus, many bacilli.
normal.cn: 单数 bacillus，复数 bacilli。

normal.en: Bacterium and bacteria follow the same rule.
normal.cn: bacterium 与 bacteria 遵循同一规则。

normal.en: A capital Bacillus means the genus.
normal.cn: 大写 Bacillus 指那个属。

normal.en: The tubercle bacillus causes tuberculosis.
normal.cn: 结核杆菌引起结核病。

normal.en: Coccus is round, bacillus is rod-shaped.
normal.cn: coccus 是球形，bacillus 是杆状。

abstract.en: Picture matchsticks scattered on glass.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃片上散落的火柴棍。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny staff under a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象镜头下一根微小的杖。

abstract.en: Think of a seed that survives boiling.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗经得起煮沸的种子。

examples.en: The bacillus was identified within a day.
examples.cn: 那株杆菌一天内就被鉴定出来。

examples.en: Several bacilli appeared in the sample.
examples.cn: 样本中出现了若干杆菌。

examples.en: Heat does not always kill bacillus spores.
examples.cn: 加热并不总能杀死杆菌孢子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：bacul「棍、杖」+ -illus「小」——一根根小棍子，就是 bacillus 杆菌；复数按拉丁语变 bacilli。

root: 拉丁语 baculus「棍、杖」的指小形式 bacillus「小棒」被博物学借来指镜下杆状生物；1870 年代大写 Bacillus 定为产芽孢杆菌属。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same little rod: any bacterium of that shape, and the one genus formally named after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一根「小棒」：任何呈该形状的细菌，以及以之正式命名的那个属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: short rods scattered under the microscope glass
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下一根根短棒似的小东西

branches.en: Rods covering a culture plate.
branches.cn: 铺满培养皿的杆菌。

branches.en: A few rods seen in a smear.
branches.cn: 涂片中见到的少量杆菌。

branches.en: Spores that survive boiling.
branches.cn: 经得起煮沸的孢子。

branches.en: A genus fixed by bacteriology.
branches.cn: 由细菌学定下的属。

branches.en: Both are named for the rod shape.
branches.cn: 两者都因杆状而得名。

intro.en: Bacillus is bacul plus the Latin diminutive -illus; the same shrinking endings give -ule and -cule in other scientific words.
intro.cn: bacillus 是 bacul 加拉丁语指小后缀 -illus；同样的缩小词尾在其他科学词中表现为 -ule 与 -cule。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is baculus, a staff, and bacillus, a little rod; Greek bakterion, a small staff, gives bacterium beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 baculus「杖」与 bacillus「小棒」；旁边的希腊语 bakterion「小棍」产生 bacterium。

definition_zh: 遗传；遗传性；（旧义）继承
definition_en: the transmission of traits from parents to offspring, or the set of inherited characteristics of an organism
core_image: 同一对父母养大的子女，身高与性格却各有差别，差别像从看不见的账本里带出来的
scene: 同一对父母养大的子女，身高与性格却各有差别。 Researchers separate the effects of heredity from those of upbringing.
sceneCN: 这里 heredity 指「亲代把性状传给子代的生物过程」（第 1 个义项：性状的遗传传递）；句意为研究者把遗传的影响与养育的影响分开。可辨识物件：并排的身高尺、两张性格记录表、家谱图、双栏表格。

senses.title: Transmission of traits
senses.definition: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 特征由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Heredity explains why siblings resemble their parents.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传解释了为什么兄弟姐妹像他们的父母。
senses.why: The word names the process itself, not the genes that carry it, which is why it pairs naturally with environment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名过程本身，而非承载它的基因，因此天然与「环境」配对。

senses.title: An organism's inherited constitution
senses.definition: the total set of inherited characteristics of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物体所继承的全部特征
senses.example: Heredity and environment interact in development.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传与环境在发育中相互作用。
senses.why: The process sense and the constitution sense share a form: what is transmitted becomes what an organism carries.
senses.whyCN: 过程义与组成义共用一词形：被传下的东西成为生物体所携带的东西。

senses.title: The study of inheritance
senses.definition: the field or subject concerned with transmission of traits
senses.definitionCN: 研究性状传递的领域或学科
senses.example: Heredity was studied long before genes were named.
senses.exampleCN: 早在基因被命名之前，人们就在研究遗传。
senses.why: The name of the process also names the subject that studies it, so heredity can stand for a field of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 过程之名也命名研究它的学科，因此 heredity 可以指一个研究领域。

senses.title: Laws of heredity
senses.definition: the regular patterns by which traits appear in later generations
senses.definitionCN: 性状在后代中出现的规律模式
senses.example: Mendel's laws of heredity describe the ratios of traits.
senses.exampleCN: 孟德尔的遗传规律描述了性状的比例。
senses.why: Once patterns were counted, heredity could be spoken of as having laws rather than merely effects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦模式可以被计数，遗传就可以被说成有规律，而不只是有效应。

senses.title: Heredity versus environment
senses.definition: the relative contribution of inherited and environmental factors
senses.definitionCN: 遗传因素与环境因素的相对贡献
senses.example: The debate over heredity and environment has softened.
senses.exampleCN: 关于遗传与环境的争论已经缓和。
senses.why: The word became a pole in a debate, so heredity often appears opposite environment rather than alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了争论中的一极，因此 heredity 常与 environment 相对出现，而非单独使用。

senses.title: Heredity as a biological force
senses.definition: the influence of inherited factors on development and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 遗传因素对发育与行为的影响
senses.example: Heredity sets limits that nutrition can only partly shift.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传设定了界限，营养只能部分改变。
senses.why: When treated as a force, heredity explains the range of possible development rather than a single fixed result.
senses.whyCN: 当被当作一种力量时，遗传解释的是发育的可能范围，而非单一固定结果。

senses.title: Heredity in breeding
senses.definition: the transmission that breeders rely on when fixing traits
senses.definitionCN: 育种者固定性状时所依赖的传递
senses.example: Heredity determines which traits a breeder can fix.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传决定育种者能固定哪些性状。
senses.why: Breeders work with heredity as a practical constraint: some traits can be fixed, others cannot.
senses.whyCN: 育种者把遗传当作实际限制来工作：有些性状可以固定，有些不能。

senses.title: Archaic legal inheritance
senses.definition: the old sense of inheriting property or a right
senses.definitionCN: 继承财产或权利的旧义
senses.example: In older legal writing, heredity meant the right to inherit.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的法律文本中，heredity 指继承权。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest layer of the word, preserved in older statutes rather than in modern biology.
senses.whyCN: 法律义是这个词最古老的层次，保存在较早的法条中，而非现代生物学中。

intro.en: Heredity was borrowed from Latin hereditas 'inheritance, heirship', from heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: heredity 直接借自拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」，其词干为 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; related forms in other Indo-European languages are hypotheses, and any PIE form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；其他印欧语中的相关形式只是假说，任何原始印欧语形式均属重构。

items.en: Hereditas meant 'inheritance, heirship'; English heredity was borrowed directly from this Latin noun rather than through French.
items.cn: hereditas 意为「继承、继承权」；英语 heredity 直接借自这个拉丁名词，而非经法语。

items.en: The word appears in English by the sixteenth century with the legal sense 'inheritance'; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在 16 世纪已以「继承」的法律义出现在英语中；确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth century heredity was reshaped into the biological term for the transmission of traits, as breeding and cell theory advanced.
items.cn: 19 世纪，随着育种与细胞理论进展，heredity 被重塑为性状传递的生物学术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century genetics narrowed heredity to the transmission itself, distinct from the genes that carry it.
items.cn: 20 世纪的遗传学把 heredity 收窄为传递过程本身，与承载它的基因区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of heres is unsettled, and the shift from legal to biological use is not sharply dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：heres 的拉丁语之前来源未有定论，从法律义到生物学义的转变也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one separates heredity from same-root words with different grammar; group two separates it from the words for inheritance, lineage and the science of genes.
note.cn: 第一组把 heredity 与同根但语法角色不同的词分开；第二组把它与继承、世系、基因科学相关词区分。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what is transmitted; heredity is the process or constitution itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述被传递之物的形容词；heredity 是过程或组成本身。

entries.definition: What is handed down, especially culture or family property; it is not the biological process.
entries.definitionCN: 指被传下的东西，尤其是文化或家族财产；不是生物过程。

entries.definition: Able to be inherited; the word describes a possibility, while heredity names the actual transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被继承；描述可能性，而 heredity 命名实际传递。

entries.definition: A person or doctrine stressing heredity as a cause of differences; it belongs to debate rather than biology alone.
entries.definitionCN: 强调遗传是差异原因的人或学说；属于争论语境，而非单纯生物学。

entries.definition: A broader word covering legal property and biological transmission; heredity is the biological process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 较宽泛的词，涵盖法定财产与生物传递；heredity 是生物过程本身。

entries.definition: The modern science of genes; heredity names the transmission that genetics explains.
entries.definitionCN: 研究基因的现代科学；heredity 命名遗传学所要解释的传递。

entries.definition: Ancestry or lineage, especially as a line of descent; heredity is the mechanism, descent is the line.
entries.definitionCN: 指血统或世系，尤指一条下传的线；heredity 是机制，descent 是那条线。

entries.tag: the general act of passing on
entries.definition: A neutral term for passing anything from one generation to the next, biological or not.
entries.definitionCN: 中性词，指把任何东西传给下一代，不论是否生物性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: heres 'heir' + -ity: the state of being inherited.
normal.cn: heres「继承人」+ -ity：被继承的状态。

normal.en: The family runs heredity, hereditary, hereditarily and hereditarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heredity、hereditary、hereditarily 与 hereditarian。

normal.en: The fixed pair is heredity and environment.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是遗传与环境。

normal.en: Laws of heredity were counted before genes were named.
normal.cn: 在基因被命名之前，遗传规律就已被计数。

normal.en: Modern genetics separates heredity from the genes that carry it.
normal.cn: 现代遗传学把遗传过程与承载它的基因分开。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible ledger that each child receives with a few entries already filled in.
abstract.cn: 想象每个孩子都收到一本看不见的账本，上面已写好几笔。

abstract.en: Picture two seeds from one pod landing in different soils.
abstract.cn: 想象同一豆荚里的两粒种子落在不同的土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of cards dealt before anyone chooses how to play.
abstract.cn: 想象一手牌在任何人决定怎么打之前就已发好。

examples.en: Heredity alone does not explain the difference between the twins.
examples.cn: 单靠遗传解释不了这对双胞胎的差异。

examples.en: Breeders rely on heredity when they select for a fixed coat colour.
examples.cn: 育种者选育固定毛色时依赖遗传。

examples.en: The old statute used heredity in the sense of a right to inherit.
examples.cn: 旧法规用 heredity 指继承权。

dict_mnemonic.text: hered（继承人）+ ity（名词尾）——继承人接到的东西 → 遗传；旧义才是「继承」。

root: 拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a current running through generations: the process, the constitution it produces, the study of it, its laws, its debate with environment, its force, its use in breeding and its old legal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一股穿越世代的电流展开：传递过程、由此形成的组成、对它的研究、它的规律、它与环境的争论、它的力量、它在育种中的用途，以及旧时的法律义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible ledger handed to each child with a few entries already filled in.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个孩子都收到一本看不见的账本，上面已写好几笔。

branches.en: PROCESS AND FORCE: transmission itself, and the influence it exerts on development.
branches.cn: 过程与力量：传递本身，以及它对发育施加的影响。

branches.en: CONSTITUTION AND BREEDING: what an organism carries, and what a breeder can fix.
branches.cn: 组成与育种：生物体携带什么，育种者能固定什么。

branches.en: STUDY: the field that examines transmission before and after genes were named.
branches.cn: 研究：在基因被命名前后考察传递的领域。

branches.en: LAWS AND DEBATE: counted ratios, and the argument with environment.
branches.cn: 规律与争论：可计数的比例，以及与环境的论战。

branches.en: OLD LAW: the archaic sense of a right to inherit property.
branches.cn: 旧法律：继承财产之权利的古老义。

intro.en: Heredity is a Latin noun built on the hered- stem; the same stem forms the legal and biological words around it.
intro.cn: heredity 是建立在 hered- 词干上的拉丁名词；同一词干构成周围的法律与生物词。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, heredity, hereditary and inherit; no prefix is involved in heredity itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、heredity、hereditary 与 inherit；heredity 本身不含前缀。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.
Hereditas is the direct source of heredity.
items.exampleCN: hereditas 是 heredity 的直接来源。
这个形容词提供了 hereditary。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成状态名词。
这一性状以遗传方式传递。
继承人在契据上签了字。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit, leave as an inheritance

definition_zh: 破产（无力清偿债务的法律状态或司法程序）
definition_en: the legal state or procedure of being unable to pay one's debts
core_image: 一张被砸断的长凳，木片散落在钱币兑换商的门前
scene: 订单断了三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。 After three months without orders, the factory filed for bankruptcy, and its creditors began to register their claims.
sceneCN: 这里指「因无力偿债而进入的法律程序」（第 1 个义项：经法院处理的破产状态）；句意为断单三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。可辨识物件：断凳、法院门牌、债权登记表、封条。

pos.zh: 破产（可数或不可数；复数 bankruptcies）

derivatives.zh: 长凳词根加「断」的分词词根 → 破产的；使破产；破产者
短语意象中的基础名词，义为「长凳、钱桌」→ 银行
否定前缀加「偿付能力」名词 → 无力偿付
基础形容词加动词后缀 → 清算
「断」的词根加名词后缀 → 断裂；破裂

senses.title: The legal status of being unable to pay
senses.titleCN: 无力清偿债务的法律状态
senses.definition: the formal condition, recognised by a court, in which a debtor cannot meet its debts
senses.definitionCN: 经法院认定、债务人无法履行债务的正式状态
senses.example: The court placed the firm in bankruptcy after the payment deadline passed.
senses.exampleCN: 付款期限过后，法院使这家企业进入破产状态。
senses.why: the word began as a broken bench, so the legal status keeps the image of a trader put out of business.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指被砸断的长凳，法律状态因此保留商人被逐出营业的意象。

senses.title: Liquidation of the debtor's assets
senses.titleCN: 变卖债务人资产以清偿
senses.definition: the procedure in which assets are sold and the proceeds divided among creditors
senses.definitionCN: 变卖资产并把所得分给债权人的程序
senses.example: Bankruptcy ended with the mill sold and the workers paid first.
senses.exampleCN: 破产以工厂被出售、工人先获清偿而结束。
senses.why: if the business cannot continue, the assets must be turned into money so creditors can be paid in order.
senses.whyCN: 企业若无法继续，资产必须换成钱，债权人才能按顺序获偿。

senses.title: Reorganisation instead of sale
senses.definition: a procedure that keeps the business running while debts are restructured
senses.definitionCN: 在重组债务的同时让企业继续运营的程序
senses.example: The airline used bankruptcy to renegotiate its leases, not to close.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司借破产重新谈租约，而非关门。
senses.why: a business may be worth more alive than sold, so the law offers a route that keeps it running while debts are rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 企业活着可能比卖掉更值钱，法律因此提供一条让它继续运营、同时重组债务的路径。

senses.title: Personal bankruptcy
senses.definition: the same legal route taken by an individual rather than a company
senses.definitionCN: 由个人而非企业走上的同一法律路径
senses.example: Personal bankruptcy cleared the medical debts but ruined her credit.
senses.exampleCN: 个人破产免除了医疗债务，却毁了她的信用。
senses.why: a person can owe more than he owns just as a company can, so the same procedure is offered to individuals.
senses.whyCN: 个人也会像企业一样欠得比拥有的多，同一程序因此也向个人开放。

senses.title: The figurative collapse of an idea or system
senses.titleCN: 观念或体系的比喻性崩解
senses.definition: a total failure of a scheme, theory or institution, without any court involved
senses.definitionCN: 计划、理论或机构的彻底失败，与法院无关
senses.example: The report described the plan as a moral and economic bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称该计划在道义与经济上均已破产。
senses.why: the broken bench can be imagined anywhere, so any total failure is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 断凳可以被想象在任何地方，任何彻底的失败便都用同一个词描述。

senses.title: Moral bankruptcy in public life
senses.titleCN: 公共生活中的道德破产
senses.definition: the loss of credibility or ethical standing of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体失去公信力或道德地位
senses.example: The scandal exposed the moral bankruptcy of the leadership.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻暴露出领导层的道德破产。
senses.why: when credibility rather than money is gone, the word still fits, because nothing is left to pay with.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的是公信力而非金钱时，这个词仍然合用，因为已无东西可付。

senses.title: The act of filing a petition
senses.definition: the formal step by which a debtor or creditor starts the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 债务人或债权人启动程序的形式步骤
senses.example: The filing for bankruptcy came on a Friday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 破产申请是在一个周五下午提交的。
senses.why: the procedure begins with a document, so the act of filing is spoken of as the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 程序从一份文书开始，因此提交的动作本身被当作事件来说。

senses.title: Bankruptcy protection and the automatic stay
senses.definition: the court order that pauses collection and lawsuits while the case proceeds
senses.definitionCN: 案件进行期间暂停追债与诉讼的法院命令
senses.example: Bankruptcy protection stopped the bank from seizing the equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 破产保护阻止了银行扣押设备。
senses.why: creditors would otherwise race to seize assets, so a court order freezes collection while the case is sorted out.
senses.whyCN: 否则债权人会抢先扣押资产，法院命令因此在案件理清期间冻结追债。

senses.title: Fraudulent bankruptcy
senses.definition: the offence of hiding or transferring assets before or during insolvency
senses.definitionCN: 在无力偿付之前或期间藏匿、转移资产的罪行
senses.example: Two directors were charged with fraudulent bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 两名董事被控欺诈性破产。
senses.why: hiding assets before the case defeats the purpose of the law, so the conduct is made a separate offence.
senses.whyCN: 在案发前藏匿资产会摧毁法律的目的，因此该行为被单列为罪行。

intro.en: Bankruptcy comes from Italian banca rotta 'broken bench', the table of a money changer who could not pay. The image reached English through French and Latin forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 来自意大利语 banca rotta「被砸断的长凳」，即无力清偿的钱币兑换商的桌子。这一意象于 16 世纪经法语与拉丁形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: A banca was the bench or table where a money changer and his coins sat in a public square.
items.cn: banca 指钱币兑换商与他的钱币在公共广场上占据的长凳或桌子。

items.en: Rumpere meant 'to break', and its participle ruptus supplied the second half of banca rotta.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「打断」，其分词 ruptus 提供 banca rotta 的后一半。

items.en: In Italian practice a trader who could not pay might have his bench broken, a public sign that he could no longer do business.
items.cn: 在意大利的惯例中，无力清偿的商人可能被砸断长凳，公开表明他不能再做生意。

items.en: French borrowed the image as banqueroute, and English took the noun in the sixteenth century in forms such as bankrupt.
items.cn: 法语把这个意象借为 banqueroute，英语于 16 世纪以 bankrupt 一类形式吸收该名词。

items.en: The abstract noun bankruptcy was formed in English on the model of French, adding the ending that names a state or procedure.
items.cn: 抽象名词 bankruptcy 在英语中仿法语构成，加上表示状态或程序的词尾。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries turned the image into a statute-based procedure with liquidation, reorganisation, protection and criminal forms.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把这一意象变成以成文法为基础的程序，包含清算、重整、保护与犯罪形态。

note.en: Group one holds words from the broken-bench image or from breaking; group two holds legal and financial terms that are often used as if they were synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是出自「断凳」意象或「打断」词根的词；第二组是常被当作同义词使用的法律与金融术语。

entries.definition: A debtor legally declared unable to pay, or the act of making someone so; bankruptcy is the state or case.
entries.definitionCN: 指被依法宣告无力清偿的债务人，或使某人如此的行为；bankruptcy 指状态或案件。

entries.definition: The institution that grew from the money changer's bench; the shared origin is invisible in modern use.
entries.definitionCN: 指由钱币商长凳发展而来的机构；共同的来源在现代用法中已看不出来。

entries.definition: A break or burst, often of a pipe or a relationship; it has nothing to do with money.
entries.definitionCN: 指断裂或爆裂，常用于管道或关系；与金钱无关。

entries.definition: To break into something in progress; the prefix means between, and no debt is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指打断进行中的事情；前缀意为「在……之间」，不涉债务。

entries.definition: The accounting state of owing more than one owns; bankruptcy is the legal procedure that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 指欠得比拥有的多的会计状态；bankruptcy 是随后可能启动的法律程序。

entries.definition: The selling off of assets; it is one form bankruptcy can take, not the whole procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指变卖资产；它是破产可能采取的一种形式，而非整个程序。

entries.definition: Failure to pay on a due date; a default can occur without any bankruptcy case being opened.
entries.definitionCN: 指到期未付；违约可以在未启动任何破产案件时发生。

entries.definition: Control of a company given to an outside officer for creditors; it is a separate legal route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把公司控制权交给外部官员以维护债权人；是另一条法律路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The picture is a broken bench: a money changer's table smashed so he cannot trade.
normal.cn: 图景是一张断凳：钱币兑换商的桌子被砸，无法再做买卖。

normal.en: The family runs bankrupt, bankruptcy, bank, rupture, interrupt, disrupt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括破产的、破产、银行、断裂、打断、扰乱。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the steps: file for, declare, protection, proceedings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出步骤：申请、宣布、保护、程序。

normal.en: The bench survives in bank, and the breaking survives in rupture.
normal.cn: 那张长凳留在银行一词里，打断的动作留在断裂一词里。

normal.en: A filing is not a closure: protection can keep the business alive while debts are rebuilt.
normal.cn: 申请并不等于关门：保护可以让企业在债务重组期间继续运营。

abstract.en: Picture splinters of a wooden bench on the stones of a market square.
abstract.cn: 想象木凳的碎片散落在集市广场的石板上。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with the shutters down but the lights still on inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店拉下卷帘，里面的灯却还亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a promise collapsing under its own weight, with no court in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺在自身重量下崩塌，四周并无法院。

examples.en: The chain filed for bankruptcy after the rent review doubled its costs.
examples.cn: 租金复核使成本翻倍后，这家连锁店申请破产。

examples.en: Bankruptcy protection gave the airline time to renegotiate its leases.
examples.cn: 破产保护给了这家航空公司重新谈租约的时间。

examples.en: Analysts spoke of the bankruptcy of the theory, not of any company.
examples.cn: 分析师说的是这一理论的破产，而非任何公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「长凳」与「断」两个词根加名词后缀——钱币商的长凳被砸断，做不成买卖 → 破产

root: 意大利语 banca rotta「断凳」：banca「长凳、钱桌」加 rotta，后者出自拉丁 ruptus／rumpere「打断」。经法语 banqueroute 于 16 世纪进入英语，抽象名词仿法语构成。同根词有 rupture、interrupt、disrupt、corrupt、abrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one case: the legal status, the sale of assets, the attempt to keep trading, the individual route, the collapse of an idea, moral collapse, the filing itself, the protection that pauses creditors, and the criminal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个案件展开：法律状态、变卖资产、设法继续经营、个人路径、观念的崩解、道德崩解、申请的动作、暂停追债的保护，以及犯罪形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smashed bench on the stones of a market square.
core.cn: 核心意象：集市广场石板上的一张被砸断的长凳。

branches.en: STATUS AND PETITION: the condition is declared, and someone must file to start it.
branches.cn: 状态与申请：条件被宣告，且必须有人提交申请才能启动。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: the assets are sold, or the business is kept alive and the debts rebuilt.
branches.cn: 两种结局：资产被变卖，或企业继续存活、债务被重组。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: a person can take the same route as a company.
branches.cn: 个人：一个人可以走与企业相同的路径。

branches.en: THE WORD WITHOUT A COURT: an idea or a leadership can be called bankrupt in plain speech.
branches.cn: 无需法院的词：观念或领导层可以在日常语言中被称为破产。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND ABUSE: the law pauses collection, and the law also punishes hidden assets.
branches.cn: 保护与滥用：法律暂停追债，法律也惩罚藏匿资产。

intro.en: Bankruptcy joins the bench of the money changer with a Latin participle for broken; the breaking root also builds rupture, interrupt and corrupt.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 把钱币兑换商的长凳与表示「被打断」的拉丁分词连在一起；这一词根还构成 rupture、interrupt 与 corrupt。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere 'to break' and its participle ruptus supply the second half of the word; banca is Italian for the bench.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rumpere「打断」及其分词 ruptus 提供该词的后一半；banca 是意大利语中的长凳。

items.meaning: the state of a broken bench

items.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end.

definition_zh: adv. 飞快地；迅速地；不停地（书面语）
definition_en: Quickly or at a fast pace; a literary adverb used of work, change or growth that continues rapidly and without pause.
core_image: 脚步不停，事情一件接一件往前赶
scene: 改造工程推进得比预期快得多。 The renovation work is proceeding apace.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：工程进展迅速、一刻不停，书面语用 apace 描述这种「快步推进」的状态。

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（副词）

senses.title: Quickly, at speed
senses.definition: at a fast speed, used especially of work or progress in formal or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度，尤用于正式或书面文字中描述工作或进展
senses.example: Preparations for the summit went ahead apace.
senses.exampleCN: 峰会的筹备工作快速推进。
senses.why: The word is a- plus pace, literally at a pace, so the picture is of legs moving steadily rather than of a sudden burst.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 a- 加 pace，字面为「以某种步速」，所以画面是双腿持续迈动，而不是突然爆发。

senses.title: Without pause, steadily onward
senses.definition: continuing rapidly and without interruption, the sense carried by proceed apace and continue apace
senses.definitionCN: 快速而不中断地持续，是 proceed apace 与 continue apace 所承载的含义
senses.example: Despite the funding gap, the research continued apace.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管经费有缺口，研究仍在不停推进。
senses.why: The prefix a- means on or in a state of, so the adverb stresses that the pace is kept up, not merely that it is high.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「在……状态中」，所以这个副词强调的是步速被保持住，而不只是步速很高。

intro.en: Apace is a- plus pace, from Middle English a pas, at a pace. Pace comes from Old French pas, from Latin passus, a step, from pandere, to stretch the leg.
intro.cn: apace 是 a- 加 pace，来自中古英语 a pas「以某种步速」。pace 来自古法语 pas，后者出自拉丁语 passus「一步」，而 passus 又来自 pandere「伸腿」。

items.en: Latin pandere meant to stretch or spread, and in walking it described stretching the leg out for a stride.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pandere 意为「伸展、展开」，在行走语境中指伸腿迈出一步。

items.en: Passus was the noun for a step or a pace, and also a Roman measure of about five feet. It gives pace, pass and passage.
items.cn: passus 是表示「一步、步幅」的名词，也是罗马约五英尺的长度单位。它产生 pace、pass 与 passage。

items.en: Old French pas kept the sense of a step, and the phrase a pas meant at a pace, at a walking rate.
items.cn: 古法语 pas 保留「一步」之义，短语 a pas 意为「以某种步速」，即按行走的速度。

items.en: Middle English wrote a pas as two words, with a- meaning on or in, the same prefix seen in asleep and abroad.
items.cn: 中古英语把 a pas 写成两个词，a- 意为「在……之中」，与 asleep、abroad 中的前缀相同。

items.en: The two words fused into apace, now a literary adverb used mainly with proceed, continue, grow and change.
items.cn: 两个词合成为 apace，如今是书面副词，主要与 proceed、continue、grow、change 连用。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against apiece, which means each, and appease, to calm; the near-meaning group lists other adverbs of speed.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 apiece「每个」和 appease「平息」混淆；近义组列出其他表示速度的副词。

entries.definition: The speed of walking or progress.
An empty area or interval.
For each one; per item.
To calm someone by giving in.
At a fast speed.
With great speed.
Smoothly and fast.
In an energetic, quick manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以精力充沛而快速的方式。

normalIntro.en: Apace is a- plus pace: at a pace, so the legs keep moving without a stop.
normalIntro.cn: apace 就是 a- 加 pace：以某种步速，所以双腿不停迈动。

normal.en: It is literary: in speech say quickly, in writing say apace.
normal.cn: 它偏书面：口语说 quickly，书面可说 apace。

normal.en: The common partners are proceed, continue, grow and change.
normal.cn: 常见搭配动词是 proceed、continue、grow、change。

normal.en: It goes after the verb, not before: work proceeded apace.
normal.cn: 它放在动词之后，不放在前面：work proceeded apace。

normal.en: Do not confuse apace with apiece, which means each.
normal.cn: 别把 apace 与 apiece「每个」混淆。

normal.en: There is no comparative: not more apace in ordinary use.
normal.cn: 一般不用比较级：不说 more apace。

abstract.en: Picture a line of workers moving without a break.
abstract.cn: 想象一队工人不停歇地推进。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner holding the same stride for an hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者一小时保持同一步幅。

abstract.en: Think of scaffolding rising a floor each week.
abstract.cn: 想象脚手架每周升高一层。

examples.en: The rebuilding of the harbour proceeded apace.
examples.cn: 港口的重建快速推进。

examples.en: Rumours spread apace through the village.
examples.cn: 谣言在村里迅速传开。

examples.en: Work continues apace despite the weather.
examples.cn: 尽管天气不佳，工作仍在不停推进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a「在……中」+ pace「步速」——一直在步速里，脚步不停，就是飞快地、迅速地 apace。

root: 拉丁语 pandere「伸腿」生出 passus「一步」，古法语作 pas，中古英语 a pas「以某种步速」合成为 apace，字面即「保持在步速之中」，引申为迅速而不停。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one kept-up stride: high speed, and the same speed maintained without a pause.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种被保持住的步幅：速度很快，以及同一速度不停歇地维持下去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: legs that never stop moving, task after task
core.cn: 核心意象：脚步不停，事情一件接一件往前赶

branches.en: A harbour rebuilt in one season.
branches.cn: 一个季度内重建完成的港口。

branches.en: Rumours crossing a village by noon.
branches.cn: 中午前就传遍村子的谣言。

branches.en: Research kept up through a funding gap.
branches.cn: 经费缺口期间仍不停的研究。

branches.en: Scaffolding rising a floor each week.
branches.cn: 每周升高一层的脚手架。

branches.en: Both keep the same stride going.
branches.cn: 两者都让同一步幅持续下去。

intro.en: Apace is the prefix a- plus pace, and the step root pass- also builds pass, passage and compass.
intro.cn: apace 是前缀 a- 加 pace，「步」词根 pass- 还构成 pass、passage 与 compass。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is passus, a step, from pandere, to stretch; the prefix a- is native English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 passus「一步」，来自 pandere「伸展」；前缀 a- 是英语本族的，不是拉丁语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pandere 是 passus 的来源。
pas 传入英语成为 pace。

definition_zh: n. 烦恼；恼怒；令人厌烦的人或事
definition_en: The feeling of being mildly angry or irritated, or a person or thing that causes that feeling.
core_image: 一只在耳边绕圈的蚊子，赶不走
scene: 楼上装修的电钻声从早响到晚。 The noise from upstairs is a constant annoyance.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里不是指情绪，而是指「引起烦扰的东西」——楼上不断的电钻声本身就是一件烦扰。

forms.label: 复数（指具体烦扰事物时）

senses.title: The feeling of irritation
senses.definition: a mild anger caused by something troublesome or repeatedly disturbing
senses.definitionCN: 由麻烦或反复干扰之事引起的轻度怒气
senses.example: She could not hide her annoyance at the interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法掩饰被打断时的恼火。
senses.why: The word descends from a Latin phrase meaning it is hateful to me, so the feeling is literally something made hateful to you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自一句意为「它令我憎恶」的拉丁语短语，所以这种情绪字面上就是「被弄成令你憎恶的东西」。

senses.title: The thing that irritates
senses.definition: a person, noise or habit that produces that feeling
senses.definitionCN: 产生这种感觉的人、噪声或习惯
senses.example: The dripping tap became a real annoyance.
senses.exampleCN: 那个滴水的水龙头成了真正的烦扰。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling noun into the name of its cause, and annoyance is a standard example: the noise is an annoyance.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把情绪名词转用为其原因的名称，annoyance 是典型例子：那噪声本身就是一件烦扰。

intro.en: Annoyance is built on annoy, which comes from Old French anui, from Late Latin inodiare, to make hateful, from the Latin phrase mihi in odio est, it is hateful to me.
intro.cn: annoyance 建立在 annoy 之上，annoy 来自古法语 anui，后者出自晚期拉丁语 inodiare「使可憎」，源于拉丁语短语 mihi in odio est「它令我憎恶」。

items.en: Latin odium meant hatred, and the phrase mihi in odio est meant it is hateful to me. The same root gives odious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 odium 意为「憎恨」，短语 mihi in odio est 意为「它令我憎恶」。同一词根产生 odious。

items.en: Late Latin inodiare turned that phrase into a verb meaning to make hateful, to trouble or offend.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 inodiare 把那句短语变成动词，意为「使可憎、使烦扰、冒犯」。

items.en: Old French anui and the verb anuier kept the sense of trouble, distress and irritation, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语 anui 及动词 anuier 保留「烦扰、苦恼、恼怒」之义，并传入英语。

items.en: Middle English took the verb as anoyen in the thirteenth century, originally for serious harm as well as minor irritation.
items.cn: 中古英语在 13 世纪借为动词 anoyen，最初既指严重伤害，也指轻微烦扰。

items.en: Annoyance is formed with -ance, and English weakened the sense from harm to everyday irritation, then extended it to the cause.
items.cn: annoyance 用 -ance 构成，英语把含义从「伤害」弱化为日常「恼火」，再扩展到指引起恼火的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against noisome, which means foul-smelling, not noisy; the near-meaning group lists other words for irritation.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 noisome 混淆，它意为「恶臭的」而非「吵闹的」；近义组列出其他表示恼火的词。

entries.definition: To irritate or disturb.
Feeling mild anger.
Causing mild anger.
Foul-smelling or harmful, not noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 恶臭或有害的，不是吵闹的。

entries.definition: The state of being annoyed.
A person or thing causing trouble.
The state of being worried and annoyed.
Minor trouble or effort.

normalIntro.en: Annoyance is annoy plus -ance, and annoy comes from a Latin phrase about hatred, not from noise.
normalIntro.cn: annoyance 就是 annoy 加 -ance，而 annoy 来自一句关于「憎恶」的拉丁语短语，与 noise 无关。

normal.en: Uncountable for the feeling, countable for causes: an annoyance.
normal.cn: 指情绪时不可数，指原因时可数：an annoyance。

normal.en: Annoyed describes a person; annoying describes the cause.
normal.cn: annoyed 描述人，annoying 描述原因。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is to my annoyance, at the start of a clause.
normal.cn: 固定短语是 to my annoyance，放在句首。

normal.en: Annoy is not related to noise, despite the spelling.
normal.cn: 尽管拼写相近，annoy 与 noise 无关。

normal.en: Noisome means foul-smelling, so do not use it for loud.
normal.cn: noisome 意为「恶臭的」，不要用来表示吵闹。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito circling the ear at night.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子夜里在耳边绕圈。

abstract.en: Imagine a tap that drips once every four seconds.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每四秒滴一滴的水龙头。

abstract.en: Think of a small stone inside a shoe.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里的一颗小石子。

examples.en: He sighed with annoyance and closed the window.
examples.cn: 他恼火地叹了口气，关上窗。

examples.en: The delay caused considerable annoyance to passengers.
examples.cn: 延误让乘客相当恼火。

examples.en: Parking fines are a daily annoyance in this street.
examples.cn: 在这条街上，停车罚单是每天的烦扰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额诺伊恩斯」——额（an）诺（noy）伊恩斯（ance）：额头上冒火，耳边「嗡嗡」赶不走，就是烦恼、烦扰。

root: 拉丁语 odium「憎恨」经短语 in odio「令我憎恶」生出晚期拉丁语 inodiare，古法语作 anui，英语作 annoy「使恼火」，加 -ance 成 annoyance，兼指情绪与起因。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one small hatred: the feeling inside you, and the noise or habit outside that puts it there.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一点小小的憎恶：你心里的那种感觉，以及外面把它放进来的噪声或习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mosquito circling the ear that will not be driven off
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在耳边绕圈赶不走的蚊子

branches.en: A sigh at the third interruption.
branches.cn: 第三次被打断时的一声叹气。

branches.en: Irritation that never quite becomes anger.
branches.cn: 始终没变成愤怒的恼火。

branches.en: A drill that starts at seven each morning.
branches.cn: 每早七点开工的电钻。

branches.en: A tap dripping through the night.
branches.cn: 整夜滴水的水龙头。

branches.en: One feeling and the thing that makes it.
branches.cn: 一种情绪，以及造成它的东西。

intro.en: Annoyance is annoy plus -ance, and the same noy- root builds noisome, while vex- and ir- build the synonyms.
intro.cn: annoyance 是 annoy 加 -ance，同一个 noy- 词根还构成 noisome，而 vex- 与 ir- 构成它的近义词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is odium, hatred, turned into the verb inodiare; Old French anui carried it into English annoy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 odium「憎恨」，被变成动词 inodiare；古法语 anui 把它带入英语 annoy。

latinEntries.exampleCN: inodiare 是 annoy 的来源。
anui 传入英语成为 annoy。

definition_zh: n. 仲裁，公断（由中立第三方裁断争议）；（合同中的）仲裁机制
definition_en: The settlement of a dispute by an independent third party whose decision the sides have agreed to accept; in contracts, the mechanism that replaces going to court.
core_image: 双方各说各话，交给中间那个人拍板
scene: 合同写明争议一律提交仲裁。 The contract sends every dispute to arbitration.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arbitration 指把争议交给中立第三方裁断，而不是上法院。

senses.title: Settlement by a third party
senses.definition: the process in which a neutral person or panel hears both sides and issues a decision that resolves the dispute
senses.definitionCN: 由中立个人或小组听取双方陈述并作出解决争议的裁定的程序
senses.example: The pay dispute ended in arbitration after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周之后，薪酬争议以仲裁收场。
senses.why: The root arbiter means one who goes to see and judge, so arbitration is literally the work of that witness turned judge.
senses.whyCN: 词根 arbiter 意为「去看并作出判断的人」，所以 arbitration 字面就是那位见证人转为裁判后所做的工作。

senses.title: The contractual mechanism
senses.definition: in law and commerce, the agreed route that replaces litigation, usually written into a contract as a clause
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与商业中，指替代诉讼的约定途径，通常以条款形式写进合同
senses.example: Binding arbitration bars either side from suing later.
senses.exampleCN: 有约束力的仲裁禁止任何一方事后起诉。
senses.why: Here the word names an institution rather than an event: the standing arrangement the parties chose before any quarrel began.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是一套制度而非一次事件：双方在争吵开始之前就选好的常设安排。

intro.en: Arbitration comes from Latin arbitratio, from arbitrari, to judge, from arbiter, a witness who goes to see, built from ad-, to, and baetere, to come.
intro.cn: arbitration 来自拉丁语 arbitratio，出自 arbitrari「裁断」，而 arbitrari 来自 arbiter「去看情况的见证人」，由 ad-「向」与 baetere「来、去」构成。

items.en: Latin arbiter named someone who goes to look at a matter and then judges it, a witness with authority.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arbiter 指去查看某事然后作出判断的人，一个有权威的见证人。

items.en: The verb arbitrari meant to consider and decide, at first neutrally, without any hint of whim.
items.cn: 动词 arbitrari 意为「考量并裁定」，起初是中性的，没有任何「随意」的意味。

items.en: The noun arbitratio named the act of judging between parties, the source of the modern term.
items.cn: 名词 arbitratio 指在各方之间裁断这一行为，是现代术语的来源。

items.en: Old French kept arbitration for settlement out of court, a practice medieval merchants relied on.
items.cn: 古法语用 arbitration 指庭外解决，这是中世纪商人依赖的做法。

items.en: English recorded the word in the fourteenth century for the decision of an arbitrator.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪记录该词，指仲裁人作出的裁定。

items.en: Today arbitration clauses sit in trade and labour contracts, and the award is enforceable across borders.
items.cn: 如今仲裁条款见于贸易与劳动合同，裁决可跨境执行。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts arbitrary, which is whim rather than reasoned judgement, and arbitrage, a trading term; the near-meaning group lists other ways to settle a dispute.
note.cn: 形近组对比 arbitrary「凭兴致而非讲理裁断」与 arbitrage「套利」；近义组列出其他解决争议的方式。

entries.definition: Based on whim, not on reason.
To judge between two sides.
A person with power to decide.
Profiting from price gaps between markets.
Helping sides reach their own deal.
A formal ruling on a dispute.
Bringing hostile parties together.
An agreement that ends a dispute.

normalIntro.en: Arbitration is arbiter plus -ation: the work of the person who comes, looks and decides.
normalIntro.cn: arbitration 就是 arbiter 加 -ation：那位「来看一看再拍板」的人所做的工作。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say arbitration, not an arbitration.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 arbitration，不说 an arbitration。

normal.en: The person is an arbitrator; the verb is arbitrate.
normal.cn: 人是 arbitrator，动词是 arbitrate。

normal.en: Arbitrary means capricious, a very different judgement.
normal.cn: arbitrary 意为反复无常，是完全不同的评价。

normal.en: Mediation helps sides agree; arbitration decides for them.
normal.cn: mediation 帮双方谈成，arbitration 替他们定。

normal.en: The result is called an award, not a verdict.
normal.cn: 结果叫 award，不叫 verdict。

abstract.en: Picture two people pointing at one line on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两人指着地图上同一条线争执。

abstract.en: Imagine a third chair placed between two arguing sides.
abstract.cn: 想象在争执双方之间摆上第三把椅子。

abstract.en: Think of a contract that quietly rules out court.
abstract.cn: 想象一份悄悄排除法院的合同。

examples.en: Both firms agreed to settle by arbitration.
examples.cn: 两家公司同意通过仲裁解决。

examples.en: The arbitration clause survives the rest of the contract.
examples.cn: 仲裁条款在合同其余部分失效后仍然有效。

examples.en: Arbitration is usually faster than a court case.
examples.cn: 仲裁通常比诉讼快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arbiter「裁判」+ -ation「行为」——请裁判来断案，就是仲裁 arbitration。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 baetere「来」成 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」，生出 arbitrari「裁断」与 arbitratio；经古法语入英语作 arbitration，指庭外裁断。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one act of judging: the hearing that settles a quarrel, and the standing arrangement that promises such a hearing.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种裁断：解决争吵的那次听审，以及承诺会有这种听审的常设安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides talking past each other, one person in the middle deciding
core.cn: 核心意象：双方各说各话，交给中间那个人拍板

branches.en: A pay quarrel closed in six weeks.
branches.cn: 六周结束的薪酬争议。

branches.en: A panel hearing both sides once.
branches.cn: 一次性听取双方的小组。

branches.en: A clause that rules out court.
branches.cn: 排除法院的条款。

branches.en: An award enforceable abroad.
branches.cn: 可在境外执行的裁决。

branches.en: Both put the decision in a third hand.
branches.cn: 两者都把裁定交到第三方手里。

intro.en: Arbitration is arbiter plus -ation; the same root builds arbitrate, arbitrator, arbitral, arbitrary and arbitrage.
intro.cn: arbitration 是 arbiter 加 -ation；同一词根还构成 arbitrate、arbitrator、arbitral、arbitrary 与 arbitrage。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arbiter, arbitrari and arbitratio; the prefix inside arbiter is ad-, to, before baetere, to come.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arbiter、arbitrari 与 arbitratio；arbiter 内部的前缀是 ad-「向」，接 baetere「来」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arbitrari 是 arbitration 的来源。

definition_zh: 纺织品；织物；纺织原料；纺织的
definition_en: cloth made by weaving or knitting, or the material from which such cloth is made
core_image: 无数细线在织机上纵横交错，最后压成一整匹平整的布
scene: 工厂把成卷的棉纱送进织机，出来时已是一整匹布。 The mill fed rolls of cotton yarn into the loom, and a bolt of textile came out.
sceneCN: 这里指「织成的布匹」（第 1 个义项：纺织成品）；句意为工厂把成卷的棉纱送进织机，出来时已是一整匹纺织品。可辨识物件：棉纱卷、织机、布匹、传送带。

derivatives.zh: 纺织产品；纺织业（由基础词加表示复数的后缀构成，语义偏移为商品类别与行业）
纺织品设计师（由基础词与表示「设计师」的词复合，语义收窄为职业）
以纺织材料为基础的（由基础词与表示「以……为基础」的词复合，语义偏移为材料属性）
类似纺织品的（由基础词加表示「像……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）

senses.title: Woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth produced by weaving, knitting or another fabric-making process
senses.definitionCN: 通过机织、针织或其他制布工艺生产出来的布
senses.example: A bolt of textile came out of the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 一整匹布从织机里出来。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to weave'. A textile is literally a woven thing, so the sense begins with the finished cloth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个意为「编织」的拉丁动词。纺织品字面上就是「被织成的东西」，因此词义从成品布开始。

senses.title: The textile industry
senses.definition: the industry that makes cloth, usually referred to in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 制造布料的工业，通常用复数形式指整个行业
senses.example: The town's textiles employed half its workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇的纺织业雇用了半数工人。
senses.why: An industry named after its product uses the plural to mean the sector as a whole, not a pile of individual cloths.
senses.whyCN: 以产品命名的行业用复数指整个部门，而不是指一堆具体的布。

senses.title: Fibre material for cloth
senses.definition: the fibre, yarn or filament from which cloth is made
senses.definitionCN: 用来制作布料的纤维、纱线或长丝
senses.example: The lab tests textile before it reaches the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在原料上织机之前先做检测。
senses.why: Because the finished cloth and its material are stages of one process, the same noun serves for both, distinguished by context.
senses.whyCN: 成品布与原料是同一过程的不同阶段，因此同一个名词兼指两者，靠语境区分。

senses.title: Relating to cloth
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：与织物有关的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of cloth, weaving or the cloth trade'
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示「织物的、织造的或纺织业的」
senses.example: Textile exports rose for the third year.
senses.exampleCN: 纺织品出口连续第三年增长。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply labels a field, so textile exports or textile design means the cloth sector rather than a particular cloth.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是给一个领域贴标签，因此纺织品出口或纺织品设计指的是布料行业，而非某一块布。

senses.title: Industrial and technical fabrics
senses.definition: engineered fabrics made for strength, filtration, protection or other technical uses
senses.definitionCN: 为强度、过滤、防护等技术用途而设计的织物
senses.example: The car uses technical textile in its seats.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的座椅用了技术纺织品。
senses.why: Modern fibres can be designed for a job rather than for appearance, so the word now covers fabrics that never reach a wardrobe.
senses.whyCN: 现代纤维可以为功能而非外观来设计，因此这个词现在也涵盖根本不会进入衣柜的织物。

senses.title: Non-woven fabric
senses.definition: fabric made by bonding or felting fibres rather than by weaving them
senses.definitionCN: 通过黏合或毡合纤维、而非编织制成的布
senses.example: The mask is made of non-woven textile.
senses.exampleCN: 这只口罩由非织造布制成。
senses.why: The category expanded past its own etymology: cloth can now be made without a loom, yet it still belongs to the textile family.
senses.whyCN: 这个类别超出了自身的词源：如今不用织机也能制布，但它仍属于纺织品家族。

senses.title: Textile design as a field
senses.definition: the discipline of designing patterns, structures and surfaces for cloth
senses.definitionCN: 为布料设计图案、结构与表面的学科
senses.example: She studied textile at an art school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在艺术学校学习纺织品设计。
senses.why: Once cloth became a designed surface, the noun named a course of study and a profession, not only a material.
senses.whyCN: 当布料成为被设计的表面，这个名词就指一门课程与一种职业，而不只是材料。

senses.title: Household textile goods
senses.definition: cloth goods sold for the home, such as bedding, towels and curtains, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 面向家庭销售的布制品，如床品、毛巾与窗帘，通常用复数
senses.example: The shop sells home textiles on the ground floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在一层卖家用纺织品。
senses.why: Retail groups cloth by where it is used. The plural marks a product category rather than any single woven piece.
senses.whyCN: 零售业按使用场所给布料分类。复数标记的是一个商品类别，而不是某一件织物。

intro.en: Textile comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'woven', built on the verb texere 'to weave'. The same verb also gives text, texture, context and tissue. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: textile 来自一个意为「织成的」的拉丁形容词，其动词是 texere「编织」。同一个动词还给出 text、texture、context 与 tissue。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin texere meant 'to weave, plait, construct'. A text was first something woven, and only later something written.
items.cn: 拉丁 texere 意为「编织、编结、构造」。最初 text 指织成的东西，后来才指写成的东西。

items.en: The adjective textilis 'woven, able to be woven' produced the noun textilis in later usage, and English took the adjective directly.
items.cn: 形容词 textilis 意为「织成的、可织的」，在后来的用法中产生名词形式；英语直接借入了这个形容词。

items.en: French textile mediated the word in the seventeenth century, when cloth manufacture was becoming an organised trade in Europe.
items.cn: 法语 textile 在十七世纪传递了这个词；当时布料制造在欧洲正变成有组织的行业。

items.en: With mechanised spinning and weaving, textile became the standard word for mill-made cloth and for the industry itself.
items.cn: 随着机械化纺纱与织造，textile 成为工厂制布以及整个行业的标准词。

items.en: Synthetic and non-woven fibres widened the word in the twentieth century, so it now covers fabrics that are not woven at all.
items.cn: 合成纤维与非织造纤维在二十世纪拓宽了这个词，因此它现在也涵盖根本不经编织的布。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of texere before Latin is unsettled, and the Indo-European root often cited for it is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：texere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，常被引用的印欧词根属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same weaving root that now mean different things; group two holds everyday words for cloth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「编织」词根、但现在意思不同的词；第二组是表示布料的日常词。

entries.definition: relating to a text or wording; it shares the weaving root but followed the written branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与文本或措辞有关的；它共享编织词根，却走了「书写」这一支。

entries.definition: the feel or arrangement of a surface; it keeps the woven image as a quality rather than an object.
entries.definitionCN: 表面的手感或结构；它把编织意象保留为一种性质，而非物件。

entries.definition: written or printed words; historically 'that which is woven', now entirely separated from cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 书写或印刷的文字；历史上意为「织成之物」，如今已与布料完全分开。

entries.definition: the words around a passage, literally 'woven together'; it belongs to the writing branch, not the cloth trade.
entries.definitionCN: 一段文字周围的词语，字面义为「织在一起」；它属于书写分支，而非纺织行业。

entries.definition: cloth or any material made by joining parts; from Latin fabrica 'workshop', it stresses manufacture rather than weaving.
entries.definitionCN: 布料或任何由部件构成的材料；来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」，强调制造而非编织。

entries.definition: the common word for woven material; it is plainer and less industrial than textile.
entries.definitionCN: 指织物的普通词；比 textile 更朴素，也更少工业色彩。

entries.definition: any substance used to make something; it is broader than textile and says nothing about weaving.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制作某物的任何物质；比 textile 宽泛，不涉及编织。

entries.definition: cloth arranged in folds as curtains or hangings; it names a use of fabric rather than the fabric itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以褶皱形式布置成窗帘或悬挂物的布；它指布料的用途，而非布料本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'to weave', so textile is literally 'the woven thing'.
normal.cn: 词根意为「编织」，所以 textile 字面上就是「被织成的东西」。

normal.en: Text, texture and context come from the same verb, which is why a text can be described as woven.
normal.cn: text、texture 与 context 都出自同一个动词，这也是为什么一篇文本可以被形容为「织成」的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the industry: textile industry, textile mill, textile production.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出行业：纺织工业、纺织厂、纺织品生产。

normal.en: The plural textiles names goods and the sector, not several separate cloths.
normal.cn: 复数形式指商品与行业部门，而不是几块分开的布。

normal.en: Technical textile shows that modern fabrics may be engineered rather than woven.
normal.cn: 技术纺织品说明现代织物可以是设计出来的，而不一定是织出来的。

abstract.en: Picture thousands of threads that only become a surface when they cross.
abstract.cn: 想象成千上万根线，只有交错之后才成为一片表面。

abstract.en: Picture a word and a cloth made by the same gesture of binding strands.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词与一块布，由同一个「把线束在一起」的动作做成。

abstract.en: Picture a material that can be flat, stiff, soft or filtering without changing its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一种材料，可以是平的、硬的、软的或用于过滤，却不必改名。

examples.en: The museum displays textile from the eighteenth-century mill.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出十八世纪工厂生产的纺织品。

examples.en: Textile workers demanded cleaner air in the spinning rooms.
examples.cn: 纺织工人要求在纺纱车间里呼吸更干净的空气。

examples.en: The designers mixed textile with recycled plastic.
examples.cn: 设计师把织物与再生塑料混用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特克斯太尔」—— 把特别细密的线一根根织成整匹布 → 纺织品

root: 拉丁 textilis「织成的」，来自 texere「编织、编结」；同一动词还派生 text、texture、context、tissue。texere 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，常见印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: fibres are woven into cloth, cloth becomes an industry, a material, a field of design and a retail category, and finally a family of engineered fabrics that need no loom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一过程展开：纤维被织成布，布再成为行业、材料、设计领域与零售类别，最后成为一个无需织机的工程织物家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thousands of threads crossing on a loom until they hold together as one surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：成千上万根线在织机上交错，直到合成一整片表面。

branches.en: FROM FIBRE TO CLOTH: the material and the finished cloth are two ends of one process.
branches.cn: 从纤维到布：原料与成品布是同一过程的两端。

branches.en: GOODS AND SECTOR: the plural covers both mill products and the trade that makes them.
branches.cn: 商品与行业：复数形式既涵盖工厂产品，也涵盖制造它们的行业。

branches.en: AS A LABEL: the adjective marks anything belonging to cloth or the cloth trade.
branches.cn: 作为标签：形容词标记任何属于布料或纺织业的事物。

branches.en: BEYOND WEAVING: technical and non-woven fabrics keep the family name after leaving the loom.
branches.cn: 超越编织：技术织物与非织造布在离开织机后仍保留这个家族名称。

branches.en: AS DISCIPLINE: design turns cloth into a subject with patterns, structures and training.
branches.cn: 作为学科：设计把布料变成一门有图案、结构与训练体系的科目。

intro.en: Textile is one branch of a large Latin family built on weaving. The same root reaches writing, surface feel and the surrounding words of a passage.
intro.cn: textile 是以「编织」为核心的一大型拉丁词族中的一支。同一词根还通到书写、表面手感以及一段文字周围的词语。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere gives textile, text, texture, context and tissue; the past participle textus is literally 'a woven thing'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 texere 给出 textile、text、texture、context 与 tissue；过去分词 textus 字面义就是「织成之物」。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词既覆盖布料，也覆盖语言。

items.example: The root appears in both fabric and writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时出现在织物与书写中。

The text runs to forty pages.

items.exampleCN: 把这个句子放在上下文中读。

items.exampleCN: 这个词最初指一条布带。
纺织品占该地区出口的主要部分。

definition_zh: n. 无政府主义（主张废除国家与强制性等级）
definition_en: The political belief that the state and all coercive hierarchy should be abolished and society organised through voluntary cooperation.
core_image: 把头顶那把椅子搬走，人们自己围成一圈
scene: 这本小册子主张用合作社取代官僚机构。 Anarchism shaped the early labour movement here.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：小册子主张废除强制性的国家机构，由自愿合作来组织社会，这就是 anarchism 的核心主张。

collocations.zh: 无政府主义与社会主义

senses.title: The political doctrine
senses.definition: the belief that coercive government should be replaced by voluntary associations and mutual aid
senses.definitionCN: 主张以自愿结社与互助取代强制性政府的信念
senses.example: Anarchism argues that order need not come from above.
senses.exampleCN: 无政府主义主张秩序不必自上而下产生。
senses.why: Greek an- means without and arkhos means ruler, so the word names a programme of doing without rulers, not a programme of chaos.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 an- 意为「没有」，arkhos 意为「统治者」，所以这个词命名的是一套「不要统治者」的方案，而不是「要混乱」的方案。

senses.title: The historical movement
senses.titleCN: 历史上的无政府主义运动
senses.definition: the body of thought, writers and organisations that carried that doctrine from the nineteenth century onward
senses.definitionCN: 自 19 世纪起承载该学说的思想、作者与组织的总体
senses.example: Spanish anarchism drew millions of workers before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战前西班牙的无政府主义运动吸引了数百万工人。
senses.why: Once the doctrine had newspapers, unions and congresses, the same word came to name a movement with a history rather than only an idea.
senses.whyCN: 当这套学说有了报纸、工会与代表大会，同一个词便转而指一场有历史的运动，而不只是一个想法。

intro.en: Anarchism is Greek an-, without, plus arkhos, ruler, plus -ism. Proudhon made French anarchisme a positive programme in 1840, turning an old word for disorder into a doctrine.
intro.cn: anarchism 由希腊语 an-「没有」加 arkhos「统治者」加 -ism 构成。蒲鲁东在 1840 年把法语 anarchisme 变成一套正面方案，把一个原指混乱的旧词变成了学说。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix that builds anaerobic and anonymous.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与构成 anaerobic 和 anonymous 的是同一前缀。

items.en: Greek arkhos meant leader or ruler, from arkhein, to begin or to rule. It gives monarchy, oligarchy and hierarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhos 意为「首领、统治者」，来自 arkhein「开始、统治」。它产生 monarchy、oligarchy 与 hierarchy。

items.en: Greek anarkhia meant the absence of a ruler, and in Athens it described a year without a chief magistrate, usually with disapproval.
items.cn: 希腊语 anarkhia 意为「没有统治者」，在雅典指没有首席执政官的年份，通常带贬义。

items.en: Proudhon declared himself an anarchist in 1840 and used French anarchisme for a positive order built on contracts and mutual credit.
items.cn: 蒲鲁东在 1840 年自称无政府主义者，并用法语 anarchisme 指建立在契约与互助信贷之上的正面秩序。

items.en: English took anarchism in the mid nineteenth century, and the word now covers both the doctrine and the movements that carried it.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪中期借入 anarchism，如今该词既指学说，也指承载它的各场运动。

note.en: The look-alike group separates anarchism from anarchy, which means disorder; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring political currents.
note.cn: 形近组把 anarchism 与意为「混乱」的 anarchy 分开；近义组列出相邻的政治思潮。

A person who believes in anarchism.
Lawless or wildly disordered.
entries.definitionCN: 无法无天或极度混乱的。

entries.definition: Support for rule by a monarch.
A doctrine of maximal individual liberty.

entries.definition: A doctrine of worker union control.

entries.definition: A doctrine of common ownership.
The rejection of all established values.

normalIntro.en: Anarchism is an- plus arch plus -ism: without rulers, as a programme rather than a mess.
normalIntro.cn: anarchism 就是 an- 加 arch 加 -ism：不要统治者，而且是一套方案，不是一团乱。

normal.en: Anarchism is the doctrine; anarchy is the disorder.
normal.cn: anarchism 是学说，anarchy 是混乱。

normal.en: Arch means ruler, so monarchy is one ruler and anarchism is none.
normal.cn: arch 意为「统治者」，所以 monarchy 是一个统治者，anarchism 是没有。

normal.en: It is uncountable: anarchism, not an anarchism.
normal.cn: 它不可数：anarchism，不说 an anarchism。

normal.en: The person is an anarchist, the adjective anarchic.
normal.cn: 人是 anarchist，形容词是 anarchic。

normal.en: Proudhon turned a negative word into a positive programme in 1840.
normal.cn: 蒲鲁东在 1840 年把一个贬义词变成了正面方案。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where nobody sits at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一场没有人坐在桌首的会议。

abstract.en: Imagine a workshop run by the people who work in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间由在其中劳动的人共同管理的工场。

abstract.en: Think of a circle of chairs with the throne removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，中间那把王座被搬走了。

examples.en: Anarchism has always argued about organisation.
examples.cn: 无政府主义内部一直在争论组织问题。

examples.en: The pamphlet traces anarchism back to the 1840s.
examples.cn: 这本小册子把无政府主义追溯到 19 世纪 40 年代。

examples.en: He studied anarchism alongside early socialism.
examples.cn: 他把无政府主义与早期社会主义放在一起研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「无」+ arch「统治者」+ ism「主义」——主张不要统治者的主义，就是无政府主义，别和「混乱」的 anarchy 混。

root: 希腊语 an-「无」+ arkhos「统治者」构成 anarkhia「无统治者」，蒲鲁东 1840 年造法语 anarchisme 赋予正面含义，英语加 -ism 成 anarchism，字面即「无统治者主义」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one rejection of rulers: first the argument itself, then the newspapers, unions and people who carried it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次对统治者的拒斥：先是那套论证本身，再是承载它的报纸、工会与人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chair at the top removed, people in a circle
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶那把椅子被搬走，人们围成一圈

branches.en: A pamphlet against coercive authority.
branches.cn: 一本反对强制权威的小册子。

branches.en: Mutual aid replacing a ministry.
branches.cn: 互助取代一个部门。

branches.en: A workers congress with no chair.
branches.cn: 一场没有主席的工人代表大会。

branches.en: A century of newspapers and unions.
branches.cn: 一个世纪的报纸与工会。

branches.en: One idea, then a body that carried it.
branches.cn: 先是一个想法，再是承载它的群体。

intro.en: Anarchism is an- plus arch plus -ism, and the arch piece alone builds monarchy, oligarchy and hierarchy.
intro.cn: anarchism 是 an- 加 arch 加 -ism，仅 arch 这个部件就构成 monarchy、oligarchy 与 hierarchy。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are Greek an- and arkhos; French anarchisme supplied the modern political sense before English borrowed it.
