definition_zh: adj. 可耕的，适于耕种的（土地）　n. 耕地；种植业
definition_en: Of land, suitable for ploughing and growing crops rather than for pasture or trees; as a noun, arable land or crop farming.
core_image: 犁能翻得动、种得出粮的那片地
scene: 这一带只剩三成土地还能耕种。 Only thirty per cent of the land here is arable.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arable 修饰土地，指能犁能种庄稼，与牧场、林地相对。

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（分类性形容词）

senses.title: Land that can be ploughed
senses.definition: of soil or a field, in a condition that allows ploughing and the growing of crops
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤或田地的状况允许犁耕并种植作物
senses.example: The valley holds the only arable soil for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 方圆数英里只有这个山谷有可耕的土壤。
senses.why: The Latin root means plough and -able means able to be, so arable literally says able to be ploughed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「犁」，-able 意为「可被……的」，所以 arable 字面就是「犁得动的」。

senses.title: Crop farming as a category
senses.definition: in British farming use, arable land or arable as a noun, the branch of agriculture that grows crops rather than raising animals
senses.definitionCN: 英式农业用语中作名词，指种庄稼而非养牲畜的那一支农业
senses.example: The farm switched from dairy to arable in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场九十年代从奶牛转向了种植。
senses.why: Once the adjective named a kind of land, it could stand for that kind of farming, so the quality word became a category word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦指某类土地，就能进而指那类农业，于是表性质的词变成了表类别的词。

intro.en: Arable is Latin arabilis, that can be ploughed, from arare, to plough. The same ancient root gives Old English erian, to plough, and Greek arotos.
intro.cn: arable 就是拉丁语 arabilis「可犁的」，来自 arare「犁地」。同一古老词根还产生古英语 erian「犁」与希腊语 arotos。

items.en: The reconstructed root ar- meant to plough, one of the oldest farming words in the Indo-European family.
items.cn: 重构词根 ar- 意为「犁」，是印欧语系中最古老的农事词之一。

items.en: Latin arare meant to plough a field, the physical act of turning the soil with a blade.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arare 意为「犁田」，即用犁刀翻土这一实际动作。

items.en: Adding -abilis, able to be, gave arabilis, of land that will take the plough.
items.cn: 加上 -abilis「可被……的」得到 arabilis，指能吃得住犁的土地。

items.en: Old English erian, to plough, is the native cousin, which shows the root reached both branches.
items.cn: 古英语 erian「犁」是本族同源词，说明这个词根传到了两大支系。

items.en: French arable carried the Latin adjective into medieval Europe unchanged in shape and sense.
items.cn: 法语 arable 把这个拉丁形容词带入中世纪欧洲，形与义都没变。

items.en: English recorded arable in the fifteenth century, and British farming later made it a noun for crop growing.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪记录到 arable，后来英国农业把它用作指种植业的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against arid, which is the opposite kind of land, and parable, which only sounds similar; the near-meaning group gives other words for farmable ground.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与表示相反地况的 arid、以及只是音似的 parable 混淆；近义组给出其他表示可耕地的词。

normalIntro.en: Arable is ar-, plough, plus -able: land the plough can get through.
normalIntro.cn: arable 就是 ar-「犁」加 -able「能……的」：犁能翻得动的地。

normal.en: The fixed pair is arable land, opposed to pasture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 arable land，与 pasture 相对。

normal.en: Do not confuse arable with arid, which means dry.
normal.cn: 别把 arable 与 arid「干旱的」混淆。

normal.en: Arable farming grows crops; dairy farming keeps cows.
normal.cn: arable farming 种庄稼，dairy farming 养奶牛。

normal.en: There is no comparative: land is arable or it is not.
normal.cn: 没有比较级：地要么可耕，要么不可耕。

normal.en: In British use arable alone can be a noun.
normal.cn: 英式用法中 arable 可单独作名词。

abstract.en: Picture a blade turning dark soil in a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象犁刀把黑土翻成一条直线。

abstract.en: Imagine a map shaded only where crops can grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只在能种庄稼处上色的地图。

abstract.en: Think of stony ground that stops the plough dead.
abstract.cn: 想象让犁当场卡住的石质地。

examples.en: Erosion has cut the arable area by a fifth.
examples.cn: 侵蚀使可耕面积减少了五分之一。

examples.en: The village lost its arable land to the new road.
examples.cn: 村里的耕地被新建公路占去了。

examples.en: They grow wheat on every arable field they have.
examples.cn: 他们在每一块可耕的田里都种小麦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ar-「犁」+ -able「能……的」——犁得动、种得出粮，就是可耕的 arable。

root: 原始印欧词根 ar-「犁」生出拉丁 arare「犁地」，加 -abilis 成 arabilis「可犁的」，经法语进入英语作 arable；古英语 erian 与希腊 arotos 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses follow the plough: land the plough can enter, and the kind of farming that lives on such land.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都跟着犁走：犁能进得去的地，以及靠这种地吃饭的那类农业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the plot the plough can turn and crops can come out of
core.cn: 核心意象：犁能翻得动、种得出粮的那片地

branches.en: A valley of dark ploughable soil.
branches.cn: 一片黑土可犁的山谷。

branches.en: Stony ground the blade cannot enter.
branches.cn: 犁刀进不去的石质地。

branches.en: A farm switching from cows to wheat.
branches.cn: 从养牛转种小麦的农场。

branches.en: Arable as a branch of agriculture.
branches.cn: 作为农业一支的种植业。

branches.en: Both are defined by the plough.
branches.cn: 两者都由犁来定义。

intro.en: Arable is the plough root ar- plus -able; the field root agr- builds agriculture and agrarian beside it.
intro.cn: arable 是「犁」词根 ar- 加 -able；旁边的「田」词根 agr- 构成 agriculture 与 agrarian。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arare, arabilis, ager, a field, and colere, to till, which gives cultivate and culture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arare、arabilis、ager「田地」与 colere「耕作」，后者产生 cultivate 与 culture。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arare 是 arable 的来源。

definition_zh: v. 分派；分摊；按比例分配（责任、费用、名额等）
definition_en: To divide something into shares and give each party its part according to a rule or standard, used especially of costs, blame, seats and resources.
core_image: 把一整块按份切开，谁该拿多少就分多少
scene: 委员会按各校人数分摊这笔经费。 The committee will apportion the grant according to enrolment.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apportion 指按某个标准把总量分给各方，宾语常是费用、责任或名额。

senses.title: Share out by a rule
senses.definition: to divide a total into parts and give each person or group the share that a standard says is theirs
senses.definitionCN: 把总量切成若干份，按某个标准把各方应得的那一份分给他们
senses.example: The treaty apportioned the fishing rights between the two states.
senses.exampleCN: 条约在两国之间分配了捕鱼权。
senses.why: The word is ap- plus portion, literally to hand out portions, so a rule for dividing is always implied.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 ap- 加 portion，字面就是「把一份份递出去」，因此总隐含着一条划分标准。

senses.title: Assign blame or duty
senses.definition: to decide how much of the fault or responsibility belongs to each party involved
senses.definitionCN: 判定参与的各方各应承担多少过错或责任
senses.example: The inquiry refused to apportion blame before the evidence was complete.
senses.exampleCN: 在证据齐备之前，调查委员会拒绝归派过错。
senses.why: Here nothing physical is cut: the same picture of dividing a whole is applied to fault, which is why the verb sounds formal and legal.
senses.whyCN: 这里切的不是实物：同一幅「分整块」的画面被用在过错上，所以这个动词听起来正式、带法律味。

intro.en: Apportion is ap-, to, plus portion, from Latin portio, a share, which is related to pars, a part. English took it from Old French apportioner.
intro.cn: apportion 是 ap-「向」加 portion，后者来自拉丁语 portio「一份」，与 pars「部分」同源。英语从古法语 apportioner 借入。

items.en: Latin pars meant a part or a share of a whole. It gives part, partial, particle, apart and parcel.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pars 意为整体的「一部分、一份」。它产生 part、partial、particle、apart 与 parcel。

items.en: Portio named a measured share, the portion handed to one person out of a common stock.
items.cn: portio 指量好的一份，即从公共总量中递给某个人的那一份。

items.en: Old French portion kept the sense of a share, especially of food served to one diner.
items.cn: 古法语 portion 保留「一份」之义，尤指端给一位用餐者的那份食物。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave apportioner, to deal out shares, the verb English later borrowed.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」得到 apportioner「把份额分出去」，这就是英语后来借入的动词。

items.en: English recorded apportion in the 1570s, used from the start for dividing costs, land and duties.
items.cn: 英语在 1570 年代记录到 apportion，一开始就用于分摊费用、划分土地与职责。

items.en: Today apportion is common in law and public finance, with apportionment naming the act of dividing seats or funds.
items.cn: 如今 apportion 常见于法律与公共财政，名词 apportionment 指分配席位或资金这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group separates apportion from appoint, which means to name someone to a post; the near-meaning group lists other verbs of sharing out.
note.cn: 形近组把 apportion 与 appoint「任命」区分开；近义组列出其他表示「分出去」的动词。

entries.definition: One share of a whole.
The ratio of a part to the whole.
To name someone to a job.
The act of sharing out.
To set aside for a purpose.
To give out as a share.
To spread among many recipients.
To mark out as belonging to someone.

normalIntro.en: Apportion is ap- plus portion: hand a portion to each person, so the whole gets shared out by a rule.
normalIntro.cn: apportion 就是 ap- 加 portion：给每人递上一份，整块就按规则分完了。

normal.en: The usual objects are blame, costs, seats and resources.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是 blame、costs、seats 与 resources。

normal.en: It is formal: in speech say share out or split.
normal.cn: 它偏正式：口语可说 share out 或 split。

normal.en: The noun is apportionment, not apportionation.
normal.cn: 名词是 apportionment，不是 apportionation。

normal.en: Do not confuse apportion with appoint, to give a job.
normal.cn: 别把 apportion 与 appoint「任命」混淆。

normal.en: The pattern is apportion something among or between parties.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 apportion something among 或 between parties。

abstract.en: Picture a pie cut into named slices.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被切成署名份额的饼。

abstract.en: Imagine a bill split by how much each person ate.
abstract.cn: 想象按各人吃了多少来分的账单。

abstract.en: Think of seats handed out by population.
abstract.cn: 想象按人口分发的席位。

examples.en: The costs were apportioned according to floor area.
examples.cn: 费用按建筑面积分摊。

examples.en: It is too early to apportion blame for the crash.
examples.cn: 现在还为时过早，不宜归派事故过错。

examples.en: The board is apportioning next year's budget.
examples.cn: 董事会正在分配明年的预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ap-「向」+ portion「一份」——朝每位递上一份，按比例分完，就是分摊 apportion。

root: 拉丁语 pars「部分」生出 portio「一份」，古法语作 portion；加前缀 a-「向」成 apportioner「把份额分出去」，英语作 apportion，字面即「分成一份份给出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one act of dividing: cutting a real total into shares, and cutting fault or duty into shares the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种划分动作：把实际总量切成份额，以及用同样方式把过错或职责切成份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one whole cut into shares, each party getting what the rule says
core.cn: 核心意象：把一整块按份切开，谁该拿多少就分多少

branches.en: A grant split by school size.
branches.cn: 按学校规模分的经费。

branches.en: Fishing rights divided by treaty.
branches.cn: 由条约划分的捕鱼权。

branches.en: Fault split between two drivers.
branches.cn: 两名司机之间划分的过错。

branches.en: An inquiry that waits for evidence.
branches.cn: 等证据齐备才下结论的调查。

branches.en: Both hand out portions by a rule.
branches.cn: 两者都按规则把份额递出去。

intro.en: Apportion is ap- plus portion, and the part root port-/part- also builds proportion, partial, parcel and apart.
intro.cn: apportion 是 ap- 加 portion，「部分」词根 port-/part- 还构成 proportion、partial、parcel 与 apart。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars, a part, and portio, a measured share; the prefix ap- is ad- assimilated before p.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 pars「部分」与 portio「量好的一份」；前缀 ap- 是 ad- 在 p 前的同化形式。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pars 产生 part 与 partial。

definition_zh: n. 车轴；轮轴；（连着车轮的）轴总成
definition_en: A rod or spindle on which a wheel turns, or the whole assembly joining two wheels of a vehicle.
core_image: 穿过轮心让轮子转起来的那根铁杆
scene: 修车师傅说后轴漏油，得整套换掉。 The mechanic said the rear axle was leaking oil and had to be replaced.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：axle 指穿过轮心、让车轮绕之转动的那根杆或轴。

senses.title: The rod a wheel turns on
senses.definition: a rod or spindle passing through the centre of a wheel so that the wheel can rotate
senses.definitionCN: 穿过轮心的杆或轴，使车轮能够旋转
senses.example: The wheel spun freely on its axle.
senses.exampleCN: 车轮在轴上自由转动。
senses.why: Axle descends from a Norse word for the same rod, kin to axis, so the core is always the line a thing turns about.
senses.whyCN: axle 出自指同一根杆的诺斯语词，与 axis 同源，因此核心始终是「物体绕之转动的那条线」。

senses.title: The whole wheel assembly
senses.definition: in vehicle work, the shaft together with its bearings and the two wheels it carries
senses.definitionCN: 在车辆维修中，指轴连同轴承及其所带动的两个车轮
senses.example: They replaced the axle after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞后他们更换了整个轮轴总成。
senses.why: Because the rod is never found bare on a car, the name spread to the whole unit a mechanic removes.
senses.whyCN: 因为在汽车上这根杆从不单独存在，这个名称便扩展到修车师傅整体拆下的那个部件。

intro.en: Axle comes from Old Norse oxull, axle, from a Germanic root also behind axis and the Old English eax, all meaning the line a wheel turns on.
intro.cn: axle 来自古诺斯语 oxull「车轴」，出自同一日耳曼词根，axis 与古英语 eax 亦由此而来，都指车轮绕之转动的那条线。

items.en: A root meaning axle or shoulder joint gave words for the pivot a limb or wheel turns on.
items.cn: 一个表示「轴、肩关节」的词根产生了肢体或车轮绕之转动的枢轴类词。

items.en: Latin axis named an axle and also the line of the heavens, giving English axis.
items.cn: 拉丁语 axis 既指车轴，也指天球的轴线，产生英语 axis。

items.en: Old English eax meant axle, the native form that later lost ground.
items.cn: 古英语 eax 意为「车轴」，是后来退让的本族形式。

items.en: Old Norse oxull named the same rod and supplied the northern English form.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 oxull 指同一根杆，提供了英格兰北部的形式。

items.en: Middle English axeltre named the beam joining two wheels, from oxull plus tre, tree or beam.
items.cn: 中古英语 axeltre 指连接两轮的横梁，由 oxull 加 tre「木、梁」构成。

items.en: The shorter axle is recorded from the seventeenth century and became the workshop word.
items.cn: 较短的 axle 自十七世纪有记载，成为车间用语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the axis family; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring parts of a wheel assembly.
note.cn: 形近组保留 axis 词族；近义组列出轮轴总成上相邻的部件。

entries.definition: The line a body turns about.
Along or about an axis.
A skating jump named after a man.
entries.definitionCN: 以人名命名的滑冰跳跃。

entries.definition: A passage between rows of seats.
A slender rod that turns.
A long rod transmitting motion.
The centre of a wheel.
A part that lets a shaft turn.

normalIntro.en: Axle is kin to axis: the line a wheel turns on, and then the whole unit built around that line.
normalIntro.cn: axle 与 axis 同源：车轮绕之转动的那条线，进而指围绕这条线造出的整个部件。

normal.en: Rear axle and front axle are the usual pairs.
normal.cn: rear axle 与 front axle 是常见的一对。

normal.en: Axle grease is a set workshop phrase.
normal.cn: axle grease 是固定车间用语。

normal.en: Axis is the line, axle is the part.
normal.cn: axis 是那条线，axle 是那个件。

normal.en: The plural is axles, not axies.
normal.cn: 复数是 axles，不是 axies。

normal.en: Axletree is the older, longer name.
normal.cn: axletree 是更早、更长的名称。

abstract.en: Picture an iron rod through a wooden wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铁杆穿过木轮。

abstract.en: Imagine the wheel spinning while the rod stays.
abstract.cn: 想象轮在转而杆不动。

abstract.en: Think of one beam carrying two wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横梁带动两个轮子。

examples.en: Grease the axle before the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途行驶前给车轴上润滑脂。

examples.en: The front axle took the whole impact.
examples.cn: 前轴承受了全部撞击。

examples.en: Both axles were bent beyond repair.
examples.cn: 两根车轴都弯得无法修复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ax（与 axis 同族，「轴」）+ -le「小部件」——穿过轮心的那根轴杆，就是 axle。

root: 印欧词根表「轴、枢轴」，拉丁语 axis 与古英语 eax 由此而来；古诺斯语 oxull 加 tre「梁」成中古英语 axeltre，十七世纪缩为 axle。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses centre on one turning line: the rod itself, and the whole assembly a workshop lifts out around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都围绕一条转动之线：杆本身，以及车间围绕它整体吊出的那套部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron rod through the wheel heart that lets it spin
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过轮心让轮子转起来的那根铁杆

branches.en: A wheel spinning on its rod.
branches.cn: 在杆上转动的车轮。

branches.en: Grease applied before a drive.
branches.cn: 行车前涂上的润滑脂。

branches.en: A rear unit replaced after a crash.
branches.cn: 碰撞后更换的后轴总成。

branches.en: Two bent units beyond repair.
branches.cn: 弯得无法修复的两套总成。

branches.en: Both are built about one turning line.
branches.cn: 两者都围绕一条转动之线构成。

intro.en: Axle is ax plus the tool ending -le; the same ax root gives axis and axial, while -tree marked the older beam.
intro.cn: axle 是 ax 加工具词尾 -le；同一 ax 词根产生 axis 与 axial，而 -tree 标记了更早的横梁。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is axis, axle or heavenly line; Greek axon gives the same idea, and Latin rota, wheel, gives rotate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 axis「车轴、天轴」；希腊语 axon 给出同一概念，拉丁语 rota「轮」产生 rotate。

latinEntries.exampleCN: axon 给出生物学中的轴突。

definition_zh: n. 服务员；看管人员；随从；adj. 伴随而来的；随之发生的
definition_en: A person whose job is to look after a place or serve customers; as an adjective, accompanying something as a result or circumstance.
core_image: 站在旁边随时准备接手的那个人
scene: 停车场的看管员在入口亭里抬手示意司机往前开。 The parking attendant lifted a hand to wave the driver forward.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attendant 指在某个场所负责看管或服务的人员。

senses.title: A person who serves or watches
senses.definition: someone employed to look after a place, help customers or keep order
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看管场所、帮助顾客或维持秩序的人
senses.example: The lift attendant checked every floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯服务员逐层检查。
senses.why: Attend once meant to wait upon someone, so the -ant ending names the person doing that waiting.
senses.whyCN: attend 早期意为「侍候某人」，因此加 -ant 就指做这种侍候工作的人。

senses.title: An accompanying result
senses.definition: as an adjective, going along with something as a natural consequence or circumstance
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指作为自然结果或情形伴随某事而来
senses.example: They discussed the surgery and its attendant risks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们讨论了手术及随之而来的风险。
senses.why: The person sense is one who stands beside; the adjective keeps only the standing beside, applied to abstract things.
senses.whyCN: 人的义项是「站在旁边的人」；形容词只保留「站在旁边」，用来修饰抽象事物。

senses.title: A follower in a retinue
senses.definition: in older or formal use, a companion or servant travelling with a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时或正式用法中，指随同显贵出行的同伴或仆从
senses.example: The bishop arrived with two attendants.
senses.exampleCN: 主教带着两名随从抵达。
senses.why: Court language kept the waiting sense alive as a noun for the people who formed the train of a great person.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷语言把「侍候」义保留下来，用来指组成显贵随行队伍的人。

intro.en: Attendant is attend plus -ant; attend comes from Old French atendre, to wait for, from Latin attendere, to stretch towards, from ad-, to, and tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: attendant 是 attend 加 -ant；attend 来自古法语 atendre「等待」，出自拉丁语 attendere「朝向伸展」，由 ad-「向」与 tendere「伸展」构成。

items.en: The root ten- meant to stretch, the reaching of attention towards something.
items.cn: 词根 ten- 意为「伸展」，即注意力朝某物伸过去。

items.en: Latin tendere meant to stretch or direct, the source of tend and extend.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为「伸展、指向」，是 tend 与 extend 的来源。

items.en: With ad-, to, it became attendere, to stretch towards, hence to give heed.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」成为 attendere「朝……伸展」，进而指「留意」。

items.en: Old French atendre meant to wait for, which shifted stretch into waiting.
items.cn: 古法语 atendre 意为「等待」，把「伸展」转成了「等候」。

items.en: Middle English took the French present participle as attendaunt, one who waits upon another.
items.cn: 中古英语借入法语现在分词作 attendaunt，指侍候他人的人。

items.en: By the fifteenth century attendant named a servant and, later, anything accompanying.
items.cn: 到十五世纪 attendant 既指仆从，后来又指任何伴随之物。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the attend family and one other -ant noun; the near-meaning group lists people who serve and one adjective of accompaniment.
note.cn: 形近组保留 attend 词族和另一个 -ant 名词；近义组列出服务人员和表示伴随的形容词。

entries.definition: The act of being present.
The directing of the mind.
Paying close heed.
A person accused in court.
A person who helps in work.
A servant on a ship or plane.
One who looks after a building.
Going along with something.

normalIntro.en: Attendant is attend plus -ant: the one who attends, or the thing that attends upon an event.
normalIntro.cn: attendant 是 attend 加 -ant：侍候的人，或伴随某事而来的东西。

normal.en: Flight attendant is the commonest job title.
normal.cn: flight attendant 是最常见的职业名称。

normal.en: The adjective sits before risks or problems.
normal.cn: 形容词用法常放在 risks 或 problems 之前。

normal.en: -ant names a person; -ance names the act.
normal.cn: -ant 指人，-ance 指行为。

normal.en: Attendance is the act, attendant is the person.
normal.cn: attendance 是行为，attendant 是人。

normal.en: Attendant circumstances is a set legal phrase.
normal.cn: attendant circumstances 是固定法律用语。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing at a booth, ready.
abstract.cn: 想象有人站在亭子里随时待命。

abstract.en: Imagine a shadow that follows every decision.
abstract.cn: 想象一道跟着每个决定的影子。

abstract.en: Think of a train of people behind a bishop.
abstract.cn: 想象主教身后的一列随员。

examples.en: Ask the attendant for a locker key.
examples.cn: 向服务员要一把储物柜钥匙。

examples.en: Growth brings attendant pressures on housing.
examples.cn: 增长给住房带来随之而来的压力。

examples.en: Two attendants carried the ceremonial lamps.
examples.cn: 两名随从捧着仪仗灯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：attend「侍候、照料」+ -ant「做……的人」——在旁边照料的人就是 attendant。

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」加 ad-「向」成 attendere「把注意力伸向」，古法语 atendre 转为「等待、侍候」；加 -ant 指人，即 attendant，形容词保留「伴随」义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep the same picture of standing beside: a worker beside you, a result beside an event, a servant beside a lord.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都保留「站在旁边」这幅画面：身旁的服务员、事件旁的结果、显贵旁的随从。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone standing at your elbow, ready to take over
core.cn: 核心意象：站在你手边随时准备接手的那个人

branches.en: A booth keeper waving cars forward.
branches.cn: 在亭中示意车辆前行的看管员。

branches.en: A lift worker checking each floor.
branches.cn: 逐层检查的电梯服务员。

branches.en: Risks that come with the surgery.
branches.cn: 随手术而来的风险。

branches.en: Two servants behind a bishop.
branches.cn: 主教身后的两名仆从。

branches.en: Both name a person who waits upon another.
branches.cn: 两者都指侍候他人的人。

intro.en: Attendant is at- plus tend plus -ant; the tend root also builds attend, extend, intend and tension.
intro.cn: attendant 是 at- 加 tend 加 -ant；tend 词根还构成 attend、extend、intend 与 tension。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tendere, to stretch, attendere, to give heed, and tensio, a stretching; the -ant ending is the Latin present participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tendere「伸展」、attendere「留意」与 tensio「张力」；-ant 词尾就是拉丁语现在分词。

definition_zh: 明确的；清楚的；直言的；露骨的；显式的
definition_en: stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing to be inferred or guessed
core_image: 折起的纸被完全摊平，每一道折痕都露出来
scene: 监考老师指着黑板上的规则说： The instructions are explicit: no phones in the exam room.
sceneCN: 这里 explicit 是「明确写明的」（第 1 个义项：完全说清、不留暗示）；句意：规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。图中可辨识物件：黑板、规则清单、手机收纳盒、监考老师。

pos.zh: 明确的；清楚的；直言的；露骨的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Fully stated: nothing left implied
senses.titleCN: 明确写出：不留任何暗示
senses.definition: expressed in clear and complete words, with nothing left for the reader to infer
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚完整的话表达，不给读者留下需要推断的空白
senses.example: The instructions are explicit: no phones in the exam room.
senses.exampleCN: 规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。
senses.why: Latin explicare is ex 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. Explicit is the sheet unfolded: every line that could have stayed hidden is now open to view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explicare 是 ex「出」+ plicare「折叠」。explicit 就是被展开的那张纸：原本可以藏住的每一行，现在都摊在外面。

senses.title: Precise and unambiguous
senses.titleCN: 确切无歧义：不给第二种读法
senses.definition: so clearly worded that it can be understood in only one way
senses.definitionCN: 措辞清楚到只有一种理解方式
senses.example: The doctor gave an explicit warning about mixing the drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 医生对混用这些药物发出了明确警告。
senses.why: A folded page hides parts of the text. An explicit wording lays the whole sentence flat, so there is no fold left in which a second meaning could hide.
senses.whyCN: 折起的页面会遮住部分文字。明确的措辞把整句话摊平，于是没有一道折痕还能藏住第二种意思。

senses.title: Open about something usually hidden
senses.titleCN: 直言不讳：把通常藏着的话说出来
senses.definition: willing to state something openly that people often leave unsaid
senses.definitionCN: 愿意公开说出人们通常避而不谈的事
senses.example: She was explicit about her reasons for leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 她直言不讳地说明了自己离开的原因。
senses.why: The verb can be reflexive: a person unfolds his own motives instead of leaving them folded inside. Openness is the human version of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指向人自身：一个人把自己的动机展开，而不是折起来藏在里面。坦率就是同一意象在人的身上的版本。

senses.title: Sexually explicit content
senses.titleCN: 露骨性内容：不加遮掩地呈现
senses.definition: showing sexual acts or nudity in an open, detailed way
senses.definitionCN: 以公开、详细的方式呈现性行为或裸体
senses.example: The film is rated for explicit content.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影因含露骨内容而被分级。
senses.why: The modern phrase uses 'explicit' for what is shown rather than implied. Nothing is folded away or concealed, and that is exactly why the label warns.
senses.whyCN: 现代短语用 explicit 指“直接呈现而非暗示”的内容。没有什么被折起或遮住，这正是这个标签要警告的地方。

senses.title: Explicit language: open swearing
senses.titleCN: 粗口直出：不加消音的歌词或言语
senses.definition: containing swear words or crude language that is not edited out
senses.definitionCN: 含有未消音、未删改的粗话或脏话
senses.example: The album carries an explicit lyrics warning.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑带有“含粗口歌词”的警示。
senses.why: A clean version folds the offensive word away; an explicit version leaves it unfolded in the open. The same contrast between hidden and displayed.
senses.whyCN: 干净版把冒犯性的词折起来藏掉；explicit 版则让它展开在外。仍是“藏”与“露”的同一组对立。

senses.title: Explicit formula: fully specified
senses.titleCN: 显式公式：每一项都写出来
senses.definition: in mathematics and logic, stated in full form rather than left in shorthand or implication
senses.definitionCN: 数学与逻辑中，以完整形式写出，而不是用简写或隐含
senses.example: The paper gives an explicit formula for the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 论文给出了解的显式公式。
senses.why: A formula in shorthand is folded up; an explicit formula multiplies it out so that every term stands visible. This is the algebraic version of unfolding.
senses.whyCN: 简写公式是折起来的；显式公式把它乘开，让每一项都立在外面。这是“展开”的代数版本。

senses.title: Explicit consent: permission in plain terms
senses.titleCN: 明确同意：法律与医疗上的明示许可
senses.definition: clear, recorded permission given for a specific act, especially in law or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 对某一具体行为给出的清楚、有记录的许可，尤用于法律或医疗
senses.example: The study required explicit consent from every participant.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究要求每位参与者明确同意。
senses.why: Consent that is merely implied can be disputed later. Explicit consent is written out and signed, so the permission cannot be folded back into silence.
senses.whyCN: 仅仅隐含的同意日后可能有争议。explicit consent 被写出来并签署，许可就无法再折回沉默里。

senses.title: Explicit memory: consciously available
senses.titleCN: 外显记忆：能清楚说出来的记忆
senses.definition: in psychology, a memory that a person can consciously recall and state
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指人能有意识地回忆并说出的记忆
senses.example: Explicit memory lets you recall your first day at school.
senses.exampleCN: 外显记忆让你能回想起上学第一天。
senses.why: What is explicit is laid out where the mind can look at it. Explicit memory is knowledge a person can unfold and describe, unlike a skill that stays folded into the body.
senses.whyCN: explicit 的东西被铺在心灵能看见的地方。外显记忆是人能展开并描述的知识，不同于折进身体里的技能。

senses.title: The old manuscript explicit: here the book ends
senses.titleCN: 古抄本收尾语：书到此展开完毕
senses.definition: historical, noun: the closing word or note of a medieval manuscript, marking the end of the text
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，名词：中世纪抄本末尾的收尾词或题记，标记正文结束
senses.example: The scribe wrote explicit at the foot of the last page.
senses.exampleCN: 抄写员在最后一页末尾写下了 explicit。
senses.why: Medieval scribes ended with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded/read out'. The word that marked a completed reading became the label for the end itself.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪抄写员用 explicitus est liber 收尾，意为“书已展开／读完了”。标记“读完”的词，最后变成了“结尾”本身的标签。

intro.en: Explicit comes from Latin explicare 'to unfold, unravel, explain', ex- 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. The English adjective, meaning 'clear, not ambiguous', is first recorded in the 1610s through French explicite.
intro.cn: explicit 来自拉丁语 explicare“展开、解开、解释”，由 ex-“出”+ plicare“折叠”构成。英语形容词“清楚、不含糊”于 1610 年代经法语 explicite 进入英语。

items.en: Explicare meant 'to unfold, unroll; disentangle; explain'. The image is physical: a folded thing is opened until its parts can be seen.
items.cn: explicare 意为“展开、铺开；解开；解释”。意象是物理的：把折起的东西打开，直到各部分都能看见。

items.en: Plicare 'to fold' goes back to PIE *plek- 'to plait, weave, fold'. The same root gives plait, plexus, complex, and the two Latin directions in- and ex-.
items.cn: plicare“折叠”可追溯到原始印欧语 *plek-“编织、折叠”。同一词根生出 plait、plexus、complex，以及拉丁语里 in- 与 ex- 两个方向。

items.en: Explicitus, a variant past participle of explicare, meant 'unobstructed, clear'. What is unfolded is also unblocked: nothing is left in the way of understanding.
items.cn: explicitus 是 explicare 的异体过去分词，意为“无阻碍的、清楚的”。被展开的东西也畅通无阻：理解的道路上没有东西挡着。

items.en: English takes the adjective from French explicite with the sense 'clear, plain, not ambiguous'. It is the opposite of implicit, which is folded in.
items.cn: 英语从法语 explicite 借入形容词，义为“清楚的、明白的、不含糊的”。它是 implicit 的反面，后者是“折进去的”。

items.en: Scribes closed a manuscript with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded / read out'. From that formula, explicit became the word written at the end of a text.
items.cn: 抄写员用 explicitus est liber“书已展开／读完了”来结束抄本。从这个固定语开始，explicit 成了写在文本末尾的那个词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the 'nothing hidden' core: explicit instructions, explicit consent, sexually explicit, explicit memory. Its mirror is implicit, in- 'in' + plicare 'fold'.
items.cn: 现代英语保留“没有隐藏”的内核：explicit instructions、explicit consent、sexually explicit、explicit memory。它的镜像是 implicit，即 in-“内”+ plicare“折”。

note.en: The first group is close in spelling or word parts; the second is close in meaning. Form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或构词成分上接近；第二组在词义上接近。先看词形，再看意义。

entries.definition: implied but not stated. In- 'in' + plicare 'fold' means folded in, the mirror image of explicit's unfolded.
entries.definitionCN: 隐含而未明说的。in-“内”+ plicare“折”意为折进去，正是 explicit“展开”的镜像。

entries.definition: to explain a text or idea in detail. It is the verb; explicit is the adjective for what has been fully laid out.
entries.definitionCN: 详细解释文本或观点。它是动词；explicit 是形容词，形容已被完全铺开的内容。

entries.definition: to use something for profit, or a bold deed. It comes from Latin explicitum 'something unfolded or settled', but its meaning moved to 'turn to account'.
entries.definitionCN: 利用；开发；也可指功绩。它来自拉丁语 explicitum“被展开或了结之事”，但词义转向“加以利用”。

entries.definition: easy to understand or see. Clear can describe a style or a view; explicit stresses that the content is actually stated, not merely easy.
entries.definitionCN: 易懂的；清晰的。clear 可形容文风或视野；explicit 强调内容确实被说出来，而不只是容易懂。

entries.definition: fixed, certain, and not likely to change. Definite stresses certainty; explicit stresses complete expression.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；不会改变的。definite 强调确定性；explicit 强调表达完整。

entries.definition: having only one possible meaning. It focuses on the absence of ambiguity; explicit focuses on the presence of full statement.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一种可能含义的。它聚焦于“没有歧义”；explicit 聚焦于“把话完整说出来”。

entries.definition: stated openly and specifically, especially in a contract or law. Express is formal and legal; explicit is broader and also covers sexual content.
entries.definitionCN: 明示的，尤用于合同或法律。express 正式且偏法律；explicit 范围更广，也可指露骨内容。

normalIntro.en: Real parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ex- 'out' + plicare 'fold' = unfold. Explicit is the sheet opened flat, with every fold laid out.
normal.cn: ex-“出”+ plicare“折”= 展开。explicit 就是被摊平的那张纸，每一道折痕都铺开。

normal.en: The same plicare gives implicit 'folded in', implicate, explicate, complexity and plait.
normal.cn: 同一个 plicare 生出 implicit“折进去”、implicate、explicate、complexity 和 plait。

normal.en: Medieval scribes ended with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded / read out'; from this the word explicit came to mark the end of a text.
normal.cn: 中世纪抄写员用 explicitus est liber“书已展开／读完了”收尾；由此 explicit 成了标记文本结尾的词。

normal.en: To make something explicit is the everyday phrase for bringing an unstated rule or feeling into the open.
normal.cn: make something explicit 是日常短语，意为把没说出口的规则或感受摆到明面上。

normal.en: Do not confuse explicit with exhibit: exhibit has habere 'hold' and means hold out; explicit has plicare 'fold' and means unfold.
normal.cn: 不要把 explicit 和 exhibit 混淆：exhibit 的词根是 habere“握”，意为举出去；explicit 的词根是 plicare“折”，意为展开。

abstract.en: A letter folded small: implicit keeps it closed, explicit opens it flat and reads every line aloud.
abstract.cn: 一封折得很小的信：implicit 让它保持合着，explicit 把它摊平，并逐行读出来。

abstract.en: A rule everyone follows but nobody says is implicit; writing it on the door makes it explicit.
abstract.cn: 一条人人都遵守却没人说出口的规则是 implicit；把它写在门上，就变成 explicit。

abstract.en: Every fold has an inside and an outside. Implicit is the inside; explicit is the outside turned toward the reader.
abstract.cn: 每道折痕都有里面和外面。implicit 是里面；explicit 是翻向读者的外面。

examples.en: The instructions were explicit: no phones in the exam room.
examples.cn: 规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。

examples.en: She was explicit about her reasons for leaving.
examples.cn: 她直言不讳地说明了自己离开的原因。

examples.en: The film is rated for explicit content.
examples.cn: 这部电影因含露骨内容而被分级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯普利说」——把折起的话全铺开、普利落落地说明白 → explicit 明确的

root: 源自拉丁语 explicitus「无阻碍的、清楚的」，是 explicare「展开、解开、解释」的异体过去分词，由 ex「出」+ plicare「折叠」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of explicit share one gesture: a folded surface is opened until nothing is hidden — a rule, a warning, a motive, a sexual scene, a swear word, a formula, a consent form, a memory, or the end of a manuscript.
sensesIntro.cn: explicit 的九个义项共享同一个动作：把折起的表面打开，直到没有东西被遮住——规则、警告、动机、性场景、脏话、公式、同意书、记忆，或一部抄本的结尾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded sheet is opened flat so that every line can be read.
core.cn: 核心意象：折起的纸被完全摊平，每一行都能读到。

branches.en: THE OPEN PAGE: a fully stated instruction or warning leaves no second reading.
branches.cn: 摊开的页面：完整写出的指示或警告，不留下第二种读法。

branches.en: OPENNESS ABOUT THE HIDDEN: a motive, a sexual scene, or a swear word is brought out instead of folded away.
branches.cn: 对隐藏之事的坦白：动机、性场景或脏话被摆出来，而不是折起来藏掉。

branches.en: THE FULLY SPECIFIED: an explicit formula writes out every term, and explicit memory can be recalled and stated.
branches.cn: 完整写明：显式公式写出每一项，外显记忆能被回忆并说出。

branches.en: THE SIGNED PERMISSION: explicit consent cannot be folded back into silence.
branches.cn: 签署的许可：明确同意无法再折回沉默里。

branches.en: THE OLD COLOPHON: explicitus est liber marked the book as unfolded and finished.
branches.cn: 古老的收尾语：explicitus est liber 标记书已展开、已读完。

intro.en: Explicit is the adjective from Latin explicare: ex- 'out' plus the plic- stem 'fold'. English builds adverbs, nouns, verbs and negatives on this stem, and the same root runs through implicit, complex and plait.
intro.cn: explicit 是拉丁语 explicare 的形容词：ex-“出”加 plic- 词干“折”。英语在这个词干上构成副词、名词、动词和否定形式；同一词根也贯穿 implicit、complex 和 plait。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' has the compound explicare 'to unfold, explain' and its participle explicitus; the opposite compound implicare 'to fold in' gives implicit and implicate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plicare“折叠”有复合形式 explicare“展开、解释”及其分词 explicitus；反方向的复合形式 implicare“折进去”生出 implicit 和 implicate。

items.meaningCN: 展开的；清楚的；明确写出的（ex- 出 + plicare 折）

items.meaning: in a clear, fully stated way
items.meaningCN: 明确地；直截了当地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 她明确否认了这一说法。

items.meaningCN: 明确性；直白程度（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The explicitness of the warning left no doubt.
items.exampleCN: 警告的明确程度让人毫无怀疑。

items.meaning: to unfold the meaning of a text or idea
items.meaningCN: 解释；阐发（把折叠的含义展开）
items.example: The essay explicates the poem line by line.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章逐行阐释这首诗。

items.meaningCN: 解释；阐释（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Her explication of the theory was clear.
items.exampleCN: 她对这个理论的阐释很清楚。
这个错误是可以解释的。

items.meaningCN: 无法解释的（in- 表否定 + 可解释的）
items.example: The lights failed for inexplicable reasons.
items.exampleCN: 灯以无法解释的原因熄灭了。

items.meaning: folded in; suggested but not stated
items.meaningCN: 折进去的；隐含的（与 explicit 的“展开”相对）
items.example: There was an implicit threat in his tone.
items.exampleCN: 他的语气里有一种隐含的威胁。

items.meaning: to fold someone into a matter; to involve
items.meaningCN: 牵连；使卷入（把某人折进事件里）
items.exampleCN: 这封信牵连了两名官员。

items.meaning: to turn something to use; a bold act
items.meaningCN: 利用；开发；功绩（由“展开、了结之事”转为“加以利用”）
items.example: The company exploited a gap in the market.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司利用了市场空白。

items.meaningCN: 复杂的（com- 共同 + plectere 编织，同属 *plek- 词根）
items.example: The problem is more complex than it looks.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题比看上去更复杂。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 展开的；无阻碍的；清楚的

definition_zh: n. 拱门通道；拱形门洞（可通行的拱下空间）
definition_en: A passage roofed by an arch, or the arched opening itself, so that people can walk through under the curve.
core_image: 头顶弯成一道拱，底下留出一条能走人的路
scene: 穿过那道拱门就是老城的集市。 Beyond the archway lies the old town market.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：archway 指拱下可以通行的那条通道，重点在「能走过去」。

senses.title: A passage under an arch
senses.definition: a walkable space roofed by an arch, connecting one area to another
senses.definitionCN: 以拱为顶、可通行的空间，把一处与另一处连起来
senses.example: We stepped through the archway into a quiet courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过拱道，走进一个安静的院子。
senses.why: The word is arch plus way, so it names not the curve alone but the road that the curve makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 arch 加 way，所以它指的不只是那道弯，而是那道弯让出来的路。

senses.title: The arched opening as a structure
senses.definition: the arched entrance considered as a built feature, whether or not anyone passes through it
senses.definitionCN: 被当作建筑构件看待的拱形入口，不论是否有人从中通行
senses.example: The archway was carved with vines and birds.
senses.exampleCN: 拱门上雕着藤蔓与鸟。
senses.why: Here attention shifts from walking to building: the same opening is described as masonry rather than as a route.
senses.whyCN: 这里注意力从「走」转到「建」：同一个洞口被当作砌体而非路线来描述。

intro.en: Archway is arch plus way. Arch comes from Latin arcus, a bow, through Old French arche; way is native Old English weg. The compound is recorded in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: archway 是 arch 加 way。arch 来自拉丁语 arcus「弓」，经古法语 arche；way 是古英语本族词 weg。这个复合词记录于 18 世纪。

items.en: Latin arcus meant a bow, and then any curved structure spanning a gap.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，进而指任何跨越缺口的弧形结构。

items.en: Old French arche named the curved span, the form that gave English arch.
items.cn: 古法语 arche 指弧形跨度，这个形式给出了英语 arch。

items.en: Middle English arche was used for bridges, doorways and the brows of a face alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 arche 同样用于桥、门洞与眉毛。

items.en: Way is native, from Old English weg, a road or course, cousin to German Weg.
items.cn: way 是本族词，来自古英语 weg「路、行程」，与德语 Weg 同源。

items.en: English joined the two in the eighteenth century to name a passage roofed by an arch.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪把两者合成，指以拱为顶的通道。

items.en: Today archway is the ordinary word for an arched entrance in gardens, campuses and old towns.
items.cn: 如今 archway 是园林、校园与老城中拱形入口的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group separates arch, the curve alone, from archway, the passage under it; the near-meaning group lists other words for a way in.
note.cn: 形近组把只指弧形的 arch 与指拱下通道的 archway 分开；近义组列出其他表示入口的词。

entries.definition: A curved span over an opening.
A row of arches along a walk.
Someone who shoots with a bow.
A main public road.
An opening that gives entry.
A grand doorway or entrance.
A way through a building.
An arched roof or ceiling.

normalIntro.en: Archway is arch plus way: the arch is the roof, the way is what you walk on underneath.
normalIntro.cn: archway 就是 arch 加 way：拱是顶，way 是你在底下走的那条路。

normal.en: Arch is the curve; archway is the passage under it.
normal.cn: arch 是那道弯，archway 是弯下的通道。

normal.en: An arcade is many arches in a row.
normal.cn: arcade 是一排连着的拱。

normal.en: Use through the archway, not across it.
normal.cn: 说 through the archway，不说 across it。

normal.en: It is countable: three stone archways.
normal.cn: 它可数：three stone archways。

normal.en: Vaulted archway stresses the arched roof.
normal.cn: vaulted archway 强调拱形的顶。

abstract.en: Picture a stone rainbow you can walk under.
abstract.cn: 想象一道能走过去的石头彩虹。

abstract.en: Imagine a courtyard framed by a curve.
abstract.cn: 想象被一道弯框住的院子。

abstract.en: Think of a doorway that is also a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一个同时又是屋顶的门洞。

examples.en: Ivy had covered the whole archway.
examples.cn: 常春藤爬满了整个拱门。

examples.en: Two archways lead into the cloister.
examples.cn: 两道拱门通向回廊。

examples.en: The archways were rebuilt after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾之后这些拱门被重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arch「拱」+ way「路」——拱底下留出的那条路，就是拱门通道 archway。

root: 拉丁语 arcus「弓」经古法语 arche 成英语 arch「拱」，与古英语本族词 weg「路」在 18 世纪合成 archway，字面即「拱下的路」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one arched opening: the route you take through it, and the same opening seen as built masonry.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个拱形洞口：你从中走过的路线，以及被当作砌体看待的同一个洞口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve overhead with a walkable road left beneath it
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶弯成一道拱，底下留出一条能走人的路

branches.en: A step from street into courtyard.
branches.cn: 从街一步跨进院子。

branches.en: Two archways leading to a cloister.
branches.cn: 通向回廊的两道拱门。

branches.en: Vines and birds carved in stone.
branches.cn: 石上雕出的藤蔓与鸟。

branches.en: Archways rebuilt after a fire.
branches.cn: 火灾后重建的拱门。

branches.en: Both are a curve with a gap below.
branches.cn: 两者都是底下留缺口的弯。

intro.en: Archway is a compound of arch and way; the bow root also builds arcade, archer and arched.
intro.cn: archway 是 arch 与 way 的复合词；「弓」词根还构成 arcade、archer 与 arched。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arcus, a bow, and via, a road, which gives viaduct and deviate; way itself is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arcus「弓」与 via「路」，后者产生 viaduct 与 deviate；way 本身是日耳曼词。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arcus 是 arch 的来源。

definition_zh: 过敏；过敏反应；（口语）反感
definition_en: a condition in which the immune system reacts too strongly to a harmless substance such as pollen or food; informally, a strong dislike
core_image: 身体把无害的东西当成敌人猛打
scene: 她小时候喝牛奶没事，成年后一喝就起疹子。 Her allergy to dairy appeared only in adulthood.
sceneCN: 这里 allergy 是「过敏」（第 1 个义项：免疫系统对某种物质产生过度反应）；句意为她对乳制品的过敏到成年后才出现。核心画面是身体把无害的东西当成敌人猛打。

derivatives.zh: 相关形容词，义为「过敏的；反感的」
加 -gen 构成，义为「过敏原」
加 -ist 构成，义为「过敏专科医生」

senses.title: An immune overreaction
senses.definition: a condition in which the immune system reacts too strongly to a harmless substance such as pollen, food or dust
senses.definitionCN: 免疫系统对花粉、食物或灰尘等无害物质反应过强的状态
senses.example: Her allergy makes her eyes water every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她的过敏让她每年春天都流泪。
senses.why: Allergy was coined from Greek allos, other, plus ergon, work: the body does a changed work, reacting to something it should ignore.
senses.whyCN: allergy 由希腊语 allos「其他」加 ergon「作用」造出：身体做了一种改变的作用，对本该忽略的东西起了反应。

senses.title: A strong personal dislike
senses.definition: an informal dislike of a thing or activity, used humorously as in an allergy to hard work
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或活动的非正式厌恶，常带幽默色彩，如说对辛苦工作「过敏」
senses.example: He claims an allergy to any meeting before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称对中午之前的任何会议都过敏。
senses.why: The medical image is borrowed for taste: the person reacts as strongly and as involuntarily as if the thing were a real allergen.
senses.whyCN: 这里把医学意象借用来表达好恶：这个人的反应同样强烈、同样不由自主，仿佛那东西真是过敏原。

intro.en: Allergy is a coined medical word: Greek allos, other, plus ergon, work, named an altered reaction, and a Viennese doctor turned it into a noun in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: allergy 是一个被造出来的医学词：希腊语 allos「其他」加 ergon「作用」表示「改变了的反应」，一位维也纳医生在二十世纪初把它变成名词。

items.en: Greek allos meant other or different, the root behind allegory and allopathy.
items.cn: 希腊语 allos 意为「其他、不同」，是 allegory 与 allopathy 背后的词根。

items.en: Greek ergon meant work or action, the root of energy, organ and synergy.
items.cn: 希腊语 ergon 意为「作用、工作」，是 energy、organ 与 synergy 的词根。

items.en: The Viennese paediatrician Clemens von Pirquet coined Allergie in the early twentieth century to name any altered immune reactivity.
items.cn: 维也纳儿科医生克莱门斯·冯·皮尔凯在二十世纪初造出 Allergie，用以指任何改变了的免疫反应性。

items.en: English borrowed allergy within a few years, and it quickly replaced older phrases describing unusual reactions to food.
items.cn: 英语没几年就借入 allergy，很快取代了描述「对食物异常反应」的旧说法。

items.en: Today allergy covers both the clinical condition and a joking dislike, with allergic and allergen built from the same stem.
items.cn: 如今 allergy 既指临床病症，也指玩笑式的反感，allergic 与 allergen 都建立在同一词干上。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the allerg- family; the near-meaning group lists other words for a bad reaction to a substance.
note.cn: 形近组保留 allerg- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「对物质产生不良反应」的词。

entries.definition: Having an allergy, or strongly averse.
A substance that triggers an allergy.
A doctor specialising in allergies.
A comparison between similar things.
An excessive immune response.
Inability to tolerate a food or substance.
entries.definitionCN: 无法耐受某种食物或物质。

entries.definition: A tendency to react strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 容易起强烈反应的倾向。

entries.definition: A strong dislike of something.

normalIntro.en: Allergy is allo, other, plus erg, work: the body working differently on a harmless thing.
normalIntro.cn: allergy 就是 allo「其他」加 erg「作用」：身体对无害的东西起了不一样的作用。

normal.en: Allergic is the adjective, allergen the trigger, allergy the condition.
normal.cn: allergic 是形容词，allergen 是诱因，allergy 是病症。

normal.en: Say an allergy to nuts, not an allergy of nuts: the preposition is to.
normal.cn: 说 an allergy to nuts，不说 an allergy of nuts：介词用 to。

normal.en: It is countable, so say two allergies, one to pollen and one to cats.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 two allergies，一个对花粉，一个对猫。

normal.en: Food intolerance is not an allergy: it does not involve the immune system.
normal.cn: 食物不耐受不是过敏：它不涉及免疫系统。

normal.en: The joking use keeps to as well, as in an allergy to paperwork.
normal.cn: 玩笑用法同样用 to，如 an allergy to paperwork。

abstract.en: Picture an army attacking a delivery of flour as if it were an invasion.
abstract.cn: 想象一支军队把一车面粉当成入侵来攻打。

abstract.en: Imagine a door alarm that rings every time a friend knocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门铃警报，每次朋友敲门都响。

abstract.en: Think of a bodyguard who tackles the postman.
abstract.cn: 想象一个保镖把邮递员扑倒在地。

examples.en: The label warns that the sauce may cause an allergy.
examples.cn: 标签警告这种酱汁可能引发过敏。

examples.en: She outgrew her childhood allergy to eggs.
examples.cn: 她长大后不再对鸡蛋过敏。

examples.en: His allergy to criticism makes feedback painful.
examples.cn: 他对批评的「过敏」让反馈变得难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿勒吉」——阿勒（aller）是「别的」，吉（gy）是「作用」：身体对别的东西起了作用，就是过敏。

root: 希腊语 allos「其他、不同」加 ergon「作用」构成「改变了的反应」这一概念，二十世纪初由维也纳医生造为德语 Allergie，英语借入成为 allergy，字面即「对无害之物起了别样作用」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are an overreaction to something harmless: the medical one is the immune system attacking pollen or food, and the joking one is a person recoiling from work or criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是对无害之物的过度反应：医学义是免疫系统攻击花粉或食物，玩笑义是人对工作或批评避之不及。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the body attacking a harmless visitor
core.cn: 核心意象：身体攻击一个无害的来客

branches.en: Pollen treated as an invader.
branches.cn: 花粉被当成入侵者。

branches.en: Skin rising in rash after a meal.
branches.cn: 饭后皮肤起疹。

branches.en: A person dodging every extra task.
branches.cn: 一个人躲开每一项额外任务。

branches.en: A joke about hating early meetings.
branches.cn: 一句讨厌早会的玩笑。

branches.en: Both react too strongly to too little.
branches.cn: 两者都对太小的刺激反应太强。

intro.en: Allergy joins two Greek roots, allo- for other and erg- for work, and the same stem then builds allergic, allergen and allergist.
intro.cn: allergy 拼合两个希腊词根：allo-「其他」与 erg-「作用」，同一词干随后造出 allergic、allergen 与 allergist。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin layer: Greek allos and ergon were joined directly, coined in German, and then borrowed into English.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语层次：希腊语 allos 与 ergon 直接拼合，先在德语中造出，再进入英语。

definition_zh: n. 军备，武器装备（总称）；（舰船或飞机的）武器系统；武装起来的过程
definition_en: The weapons and military resources of a country or force; the guns and missile systems fitted to a ship or aircraft; the process of arming for war.
core_image: 把武器一件件装到船上、机上、国库里
scene: 条约限制重型军备的部署。 The treaty limits the deployment of heavy armament.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armament 指一国或一支力量的武器与军力总称。

senses.title: A country's military resources
senses.definition: the whole stock of weapons, vehicles and equipment a state or force maintains
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或一支武装力量所维持的全部武器、载具与装备
senses.example: The report compares the armament of the two alliances.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了两大同盟的军备。
senses.why: The suffix -ment names means or result, so armament is what arming produces: the equipment itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 表手段或结果，所以 armament 就是「武装」所产出的东西：装备本身。

senses.title: The guns fitted to a vessel
senses.definition: the specific guns, cannon or missile systems mounted on a ship, aircraft or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 安装在舰船、飞机或车辆上的具体火炮、舰炮或导弹系统
senses.example: The cruiser's main armament was removed after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘巡洋舰的主炮系统在战后被拆除。
senses.why: Here the word narrows from a nation to one hull: the same equipping idea applied to a single platform.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从一国收窄到一条船：同样的「装备」概念用在单个平台上。

senses.title: The act of arming
senses.definition: the process of building up military strength, the sense behind armament race
senses.definitionCN: 扩充军力的过程，即 armament race 背后的含义
senses.example: Rapid armament followed the breakdown of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判破裂之后迅速展开了军备扩充。
senses.why: Because -ment can name an action as well as its result, the word also covers the building up, not only the stock.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ment 既可表结果也可表动作，这个词也涵盖「扩充」本身，而不只是存量。

intro.en: Armament is Latin armamentum, equipment, from armare, to arm, plus the means suffix -mentum. English first used it for the guns of a warship.
intro.cn: armament 就是拉丁语 armamentum「装备」，由 armare「武装」加表手段的后缀 -mentum 构成。英语最初用它指战舰的火炮。

items.en: Latin arma meant weapons and gear, the base of arm, army, armour and armada.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arma 意为武器与装备，是 arm、army、armour 与 armada 的共同基础。

items.en: Armare meant to equip for fighting, whether a soldier, a ship or a fortress.
items.cn: armare 意为「为作战而装备」，对象可以是士兵、船只或堡垒。

items.en: Adding -mentum, the suffix for a means or instrument, gave armamentum, the equipment itself.
items.cn: 加上表手段或工具的后缀 -mentum 得到 armamentum，即装备本身。

items.en: English recorded armament in the 1690s for the guns carried by a warship.
items.cn: 英语在 1690 年代记录 armament，指战舰所携火炮。

items.en: Through the eighteenth century the word widened from one ship's guns to a whole state's military stock.
items.cn: 整个 18 世纪，词义从一条船的火炮扩展到一国全部的军事存量。

items.en: Twentieth-century treaties made armament and disarmament standard terms of international law.
items.cn: 20 世纪的条约使 armament 与 disarmament 成为国际法的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts armistice, a stop to fighting, with armament, the means of it; the near-meaning group lists other words for weapons.
note.cn: 形近组把 armistice「停战」与 armament「作战手段」对照；近义组列出其他表示武器的词。

entries.definition: An agreed stop to fighting.
Covering that stops weapons.
The rotating part of a motor.
A large fleet of warships.
Weapons considered together.
Ammunition and military stores.
Mounted guns and their supplies.
A store of weapons, or the place.

normalIntro.en: Armament is arm plus -ment: what arming produces, the equipment a force actually holds.
normalIntro.cn: armament 就是 arm 加 -ment：「武装」产出的东西，即一支力量实际持有的装备。

normal.en: Armament arms you; armistice stops the fighting.
normal.cn: armament 是武装，armistice 是停战。

normal.en: Disarmament is the reverse, with dis- added.
normal.cn: disarmament 是反向，加了 dis-。

normal.en: Main armament is the fixed naval term.
normal.cn: main armament 是海军固定术语。

normal.en: It can be countable when meaning systems.
normal.cn: 指武器系统时可数。

normal.en: Armament race and arms race mean the same thing.
normal.cn: armament race 与 arms race 同义。

abstract.en: Picture guns being bolted onto a deck.
abstract.cn: 想象火炮被螺栓固定到甲板上。

abstract.en: Imagine a warehouse counted line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象一间被逐行清点的库房。

abstract.en: Think of two states stacking weight on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两国在天平两端不断加砝码。

examples.en: The ship carried a modest armament for its size.
examples.cn: 以吨位而言，这艘船的武器配置不算多。

examples.en: Both sides pledged to cut their armaments.
examples.cn: 双方承诺削减各自军备。

examples.en: The treaty froze further armament in the region.
examples.cn: 条约冻结了该地区的进一步军备扩充。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arm「武器」+ -ment「手段、结果」——武装出来的装备，就是军备 armament。

root: 拉丁语 arma「武器」生出 armare「武装」，加表手段的后缀 -mentum 成 armamentum「装备」；英语 1690 年代先指舰炮，后扩展为一国军备。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses follow one equipping: the stock a nation holds, the guns on one hull, and the act of building the stock up.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项沿着同一次「装备」展开：一国持有的存量、一条船上的火炮，以及把存量堆起来的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weapons being fitted one by one onto ships, planes and into stores
core.cn: 核心意象：把武器一件件装到船上、机上、国库里

branches.en: Two alliances counted weapon by weapon.
branches.cn: 逐件清点武器的两大同盟。

branches.en: A cruiser stripped of its main guns.
branches.cn: 主炮被拆掉的巡洋舰。

branches.en: Missiles fitted under a wing.
branches.cn: 挂在机翼下的导弹。

branches.en: Rapid build-up after talks collapse.
branches.cn: 谈判破裂后的迅速扩充。

branches.en: Both name what arming produces.
branches.cn: 两者都指「武装」所产出的东西。

intro.en: Armament is arm plus -ment, and with dis- it flips to disarm and disarmament; the root also builds armour and army.
intro.cn: armament 是 arm 加 -ment，加上 dis- 就翻转为 disarm 与 disarmament；同一词根还构成 armour 与 army。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arma, armare and armamentum; -mentum is the Latin suffix for a means or instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arma、armare 与 armamentum；-mentum 是拉丁语表手段或工具的后缀。

definition_zh: 假设；假说；前提；待验证的猜想
definition_en: a proposed explanation or premise that is put forward as a starting point and still has to be tested or proved
core_image: 先在下面垫一块地基，再把论点垒在上面
scene: 实验室的白板上写着一句可以被实验推翻的预测，旁边是涂层样本。 Before the experiment began, the team wrote one sentence on the whiteboard: the new coating should halve the rate of corrosion. That sentence was their hypothesis.
sceneCN: 这里 hypothesis 是「科学假说」（第 1 个义项：提出一个可检验的候选解释）；句意：实验开始前，团队在白板上写下一句话：新涂层应能把腐蚀速度减半。这句话就是他们的假说。

pos.zh: 假设；假说（尤指可检验的科学解释）
前提；被当作论证起点的命题

forms.label: 名词复数（希腊语式，-is 变 -es）

derivatives.zh: 假设的（较少用，与 hypothetical 同义）

senses.title: Scientific hypothesis: a testable explanation
senses.titleCN: 科学假说：可被检验的解释
senses.definition: a proposed explanation for observed facts that can be tested by experiment or further evidence
senses.definitionCN: 针对观察到的事实提出的解释，可通过实验或进一步证据来检验
senses.example: The hypothesis that the coating slows corrosion will be tested on twenty steel plates.
senses.exampleCN: “涂层能减缓腐蚀”这一假说将在二十块钢板上接受检验。
senses.why: A hypothesis is laid under a question the way a foundation is laid under a building: it is put in place first, and the experiment is built on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 假说被垫在一个问题下面，就像地基被垫在房屋下面：它先被放好，实验再在它上面搭建。

senses.title: Logical premise: assumed as a base
senses.titleCN: 逻辑前提：被当作论证底座
senses.definition: a proposition taken as true for the sake of an argument, so that other statements can be built on it
senses.definitionCN: 为了进行论证而被当作真的命题，其他陈述可建立在它之上
senses.example: The proof rests on the hypothesis that every finite set has a largest element.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明建立在“每个有限集都有最大元素”这一前提之上。
senses.why: In logic the word keeps its Greek shape: something is placed underneath the reasoning and left there while the argument stands on it.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学里，这个词保留了希腊语的形态：某物被放在推理的下方并留在那里，论证则站在它上面。

senses.title: Everyday conjecture: an unproved guess
senses.titleCN: 日常猜想：未经证实的推测
senses.definition: a guess or suggestion offered without enough evidence, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常言谈中在证据不足时提出的猜测或设想
senses.example: My hypothesis is that the keys are still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜钥匙还在车里。
senses.why: The scientific word has loosened into daily use: any explanation put forward before proof counts as a hypothesis, even when no experiment will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个科学词已经松动到日常用法里：任何在证实之前提出的解释都算假设，即使后面并不会做实验。

senses.title: Working hypothesis: a temporary guide
senses.titleCN: 工作假设：临时的行动依据
senses.definition: a provisional explanation accepted for the time being because it guides investigation, even if it may later be replaced
senses.definitionCN: 因能指导调查而暂时接受的解释，即使以后可能被替换
senses.example: As a working hypothesis, we assume the leak comes from the north pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 作为工作假设，我们先假定泄漏来自北侧管道。
senses.why: A foundation can be temporary. The working hypothesis is laid down not because it is proved, but because building can start on it today.
senses.whyCN: 地基可以是临时的。工作假设之所以被铺下，不是因为它已被证明，而是因为今天就能在它上面开工。

senses.title: Statistics: the null hypothesis
senses.definition: in statistics, the default proposition that there is no effect or no difference, which a test tries to reject
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中默认“没有效应、没有差异”的命题，检验试图将它推翻
senses.example: The null hypothesis states that the two groups perform equally well.
senses.exampleCN: 原假设称两组表现同样好。
senses.why: Here the word is used backwards: the hypothesis laid underneath the test is the dull one, and the whole apparatus is built to knock it down.
senses.whyCN: 这里的用法是反向的：垫在检验下面的假设是最平淡的那一个，整套装置却是为了把它推倒而搭起来的。

senses.title: Plural hypotheses: rival explanations
senses.titleCN: 复数假说：并排的候选解释
senses.definition: the plural form hypotheses, used when several candidate explanations are held side by side
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 hypotheses，用于同时持有多个候选解释时
senses.example: The team listed three hypotheses and designed one test to separate them.
senses.exampleCN: 团队列出三个假说，并设计了一项能区分它们的检验。
senses.why: The Greek plural keeps the original -is to -es shift. Once several foundations are laid, the question is which one the evidence will stand on.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语式复数保留了 -is 变 -es 的变化。一旦铺下好几块地基，问题就变成证据会站在哪一块上。

senses.title: Mathematics: a conjecture awaiting proof
senses.definition: in mathematics, a statement believed to be true but not yet proved, such as a named conjecture
senses.definitionCN: 数学中相信为真但尚未证明的陈述，如以人名命名的猜想
senses.example: The Riemann hypothesis has resisted proof for more than a century.
senses.exampleCN: 黎曼猜想已有一个多世纪未能被证明。
senses.why: The mathematical hypothesis is a foundation laid under a whole building that does not yet exist: if it holds, a large structure of proofs can be raised.
senses.whyCN: 数学猜想是垫在一整座尚未存在的建筑下面的地基：只要它成立，一大片证明就能被垒起来。

senses.title: On the hypothesis that: a supposition for argument
senses.titleCN: 以假设为前提：为了推论而假定
senses.definition: in the phrase 'on the hypothesis that', used to grant a supposition temporarily and then reason from it
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 on the hypothesis that 中，暂时承认某一设想并由此推理
senses.example: On the hypothesis that demand stays flat, the new factory would still lose money.
senses.exampleCN: 假定需求保持不变，新工厂仍然会亏损。
senses.why: The phrase marks the foundation being laid on purpose: everyone agrees to stand on it for the length of the argument, and no longer.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标记的是有意铺下的地基：大家同意在论证期间站上去，论证一结束就不再站了。

senses.title: Original sense: a groundwork
senses.definition: in the earliest English use, a particular statement or groundwork on which other statements rest
senses.definitionCN: 在最早的英语用法中，指承载其他陈述的某一说法或基础
senses.example: The old logic text calls the first principle the hypothesis of the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧逻辑教材把第一原理称为整个论证的基础。
senses.why: Greek hypothesis literally meant 'a placing under', the base or groundwork of a building. The logical sense grew from that physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hypothesis 字面意为“放在下面”，即建筑的地基或底座。逻辑义正是从这幅物理画面长出来的。

intro.en: Hypothesis is a Greek word borrowed through French and Latin, and its parts are still visible: hypo- 'under' plus thesis 'a placing'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hypothesis 是经法语和拉丁语借入的希腊词，构词成分至今可见：hypo-“在下”加 thesis“放置”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'a particular statement'. The word entered through French hypothese and directly from Late Latin hypothesis.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，意为“某一具体陈述”。这个词经法语 hypothese 并直接由晚期拉丁语 hypothesis 进入英语。

items.en: The sense 'a proposition assumed and taken for granted, used as a premise' is recorded, the sense that still governs logic and argument.
items.cn: 记录到“被假定并视为当然、用作前提的命题”这一义项，这也是至今支配逻辑与论证的义项。

items.en: Greek hypothesis meant 'base, groundwork, foundation', and in extended use 'basis of an argument, supposition', literally 'a placing under'.
items.cn: 希腊语 hypothesis 意为“底座、地基、基础”，引申为“论证的基础、设想”，字面即“放在下面”。

items.en: The word joins hypo- 'under' and thesis 'a placing, proposition'. Thesis goes back to a reduplicated form of PIE *dhe- 'to set, put', the root also behind do, deed, and theme.
items.cn: 这个词由 hypo-“在下”与 thesis“放置、命题”组合而成。thesis 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置、安放”的重复形式，该词根也是 do、deed、theme 的来源。

items.en: The narrower scientific sense, an explanation to be tested, is recorded. From this point the word belongs to experiment as much as to logic.
items.cn: 较窄的科学义“待检验的解释”有记录。自此这个词既属于逻辑，也属于实验。

items.en: The Greek plural hypotheses is kept unchanged, unlike most English nouns. Hypothetical (1580s) and hypothesize (1738) build the rest of the family; theory and thesis remain distinct neighbours.
items.cn: 希腊语式复数 hypotheses 原样保留，与大多数英语名词不同。hypothetical（16 世纪 80 年代）与 hypothesize（1738）补足了词族；theory 与 thesis 仍是各自独立的邻词。

note.en: The first group separates the plural, the adjective, and the verb built on hypothesis; the second group compares words for explanations and for premises.
note.cn: 第一组把复数、形容词和由 hypothesis 构成的动词分开；第二组比较表示“解释”与“前提”的词。

entries.definition: the plural of hypothesis, not a different word. Greek nouns in -is regularly become -es, so one hypothesis becomes two hypotheses.
entries.definitionCN: hypothesis 的复数，不是另一个词。以 -is 结尾的希腊语名词通常变 -es，所以一个假说变成两个假说。

entries.definition: based on a hypothesis or imagined for the sake of argument. It describes a situation, not a scientific claim, and is often close to 'imaginary'.
entries.definitionCN: 基于假设的，或为论证而设想的。它描述一种情形，而不是一条科学主张，常接近“虚构的”。

entries.definition: to form a hypothesis. The verb names the act of laying the foundation; the noun names the foundation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 提出假说。动词命名“铺地基”的动作，名词命名地基本身。

entries.definition: a coherent set of principles that explains a broad class of facts. A theory is a finished building; a hypothesis is the foundation stone laid before the building is tested.
entries.definitionCN: 解释一大类事实的连贯原理体系。theory 是建成的房屋；hypothesis 是房屋受检前铺下的奠基石。

entries.definition: a proposition put forward and defended in argument, or a long research essay. It shares Greek thesis 'a placing' with hypothesis, but stands on its own rather than under something else.
entries.definitionCN: 在论证中提出并加以辩护的命题，或长篇研究论文。它与 hypothesis 共享希腊语 thesis“放置”，但它是自己站着的，而不是垫在别物之下。

entries.definition: something assumed to be true for the sake of reasoning. It is a near translation of Greek hypothesis and carries less scientific weight.
entries.definitionCN: 为推理而假定为真的事。它几乎是希腊语 hypothesis 的译法，科学分量更轻。

entries.definition: an opinion formed from incomplete evidence. A conjecture is openly a guess; a hypothesis is a guess set up so that it can be tested.
entries.definitionCN: 根据不完整证据形成的看法。conjecture 明说是猜测；hypothesis 则是为了让其可被检验而搭起来的猜测。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: hypo- 'under', thesis 'a placing', the Greek plural hypotheses, and the family hypothetical / hypothesize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：hypo-“在下”、thesis“放置”、希腊语式复数 hypotheses，以及 hypothetical／hypothesize 词族。

normal.en: hypo- means 'under' and thesis means 'a placing'. A hypothesis is something placed under a question so that reasoning can stand on it.
normal.cn: hypo- 表示“在下”，thesis 表示“放置”。hypothesis 就是被放在问题下面、让推理可以站上去的东西。

normal.en: The plural is hypotheses, not hypothesises: Greek -is becomes -es, as in analysis and basis.
normal.cn: 复数是 hypotheses，不是 hypothesises：希腊语式 -is 变 -es，如 analysis、basis 一样。

normal.en: Hypothetical means 'assumed for the sake of argument', and hypothesize means 'to lay that foundation down'.
normal.cn: hypothetical 意为“为论证而假设的”，hypothesize 意为“把这块地基铺下去”。

normal.en: A hypothesis and a thesis share thesis 'a placing', but a thesis stands up to be defended while a hypothesis lies underneath to be tested.
normal.cn: hypothesis 与 thesis 共享 thesis“放置”，但 thesis 立起来供人辩护，hypothesis 则躺在下面等着被检验。

normal.en: The null hypothesis is the dull foundation: it says there is no effect, and the experiment is built to knock it down.
normal.cn: 原假设是最平淡的地基：它宣称没有效应，而实验正是为了把它推倒而搭起来的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone slab laid in soft ground. Nothing is built yet, and the slab may sink or hold, but every later brick depends on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板被铺进软土里。上面还没有建筑，石板可能下沉也可能撑住，但后来的每一块砖都依赖它。

abstract.en: A hypothesis is a bet you can lose: the good ones are laid where a test can reach them, not where they are safe from evidence.
abstract.cn: 假说是一场你可以输掉的赌：好的假说被铺在检验够得着的地方，而不是铺在证据碰不到的安全角落。

abstract.en: When several foundations lie side by side, the experiment is not looking for support but for separation: which slab alone can carry the building?
abstract.cn: 当好几块地基并排铺着，实验要找的不是支撑而是区分：哪一块独自能承起这座建筑？

examples.en: Every experiment begins with a hypothesis, but few survive the first week.
examples.cn: 每个实验都从一个假说开始，但很少有假说能熬过第一周。

examples.en: She treated the rumour as a working hypothesis and went to check the records.
examples.cn: 她把这个传闻当作工作假设，然后去查记录。

examples.en: The two hypotheses predict different results, which is exactly why the test is worth running.
examples.cn: 两个假说预测出不同的结果，这正是这项检验值得做的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: “嗨，破塞西斯”——嗨，先破开地面、塞一块石板在下面当底座，上面再放待验的想法 → hypothesis 假设、前提

root: 源自希腊语 hypothesis“垫在下面的地基”，由 hypo-“在下”+ thesis“放置”构成，核心是“先垫一块地基，让论点立在上面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of hypothesis, all from one gesture: something is placed underneath — a question, an argument, a test, a proof — so that reasoning can stand on it and later be knocked down.
sensesIntro.cn: hypothesis 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把某物垫在下面——问题、论证、检验、证明——让推理站上去，并在以后被推倒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slab laid under a structure that is still to be built and tested.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石板铺在尚待建造、尚待检验的结构之下。

branches.en: TESTABLE CLAIMS: science and mathematics lay a claim underneath and then try to break it with evidence or proof.
branches.cn: 可检验的主张：科学与数学把一条主张垫在下面，再用证据或证明去击打它。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: logic, argumentative supposition, and the oldest sense all keep the literal groundwork.
branches.cn: 地基：逻辑前提、论证中的假定与最古老的义项，都保留了字面上的“垫在下面”。

branches.en: GUESS AND TOOL: daily conjecture has no test attached, while a working hypothesis is laid down so that work can start today.
branches.cn: 猜想与工具：日常猜测后面没有检验，而工作假设被铺下是为了今天就能开工。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the null hypothesis is the plain foundation that the whole test is built to demolish.
branches.cn: 统计学：原假设是最朴素的地基，整套检验却是为了拆掉它而建。

branches.en: RIVALS: several hypotheses stand side by side, and the evidence must choose which slab to stand on.
branches.cn: 竞争者：多个假说并排而立，证据必须选择站上哪一块石板。

intro.en: Hypothesis is a Greek compound borrowed whole: hypo- 'under' plus thesis 'a placing'. English adds -ical, -ly, and -ize, and the same two Greek pieces build a large family.
intro.cn: hypothesis 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：hypo-“在下”加 thesis“放置”。英语加上 -ical、-ly、-ize，同样两个希腊成分还构成一大群词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin took the Greek word unchanged as hypothesis, and Latin thesis came from the same Greek noun. Medieval Latin suppositio was used to translate hypothesis, which is why supposition still feels like its twin.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语原样吸收了希腊词 hypothesis，拉丁语 thesis 也来自同一个希腊名词。中世纪拉丁语用 suppositio 翻译 hypothesis，所以 supposition 至今像是它的双胞胎。

items.meaning: a proposition placed under an argument; a testable explanation
items.meaningCN: 垫在论证下面的命题；可检验的解释（hypo- 在下 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The hypothesis was rejected after the second trial.
items.exampleCN: 第二次试验之后，这个假说被否定了。

items.meaningCN: 两个或更多假说（希腊语式复数 -es）
items.example: Both hypotheses assume the same starting temperature.
items.exampleCN: 两个假说都假定相同的初始温度。

items.meaning: based on a hypothesis; imagined for argument
items.meaningCN: 假设的；为论证而假想的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: Consider a hypothetical case in which no one answers.
items.exampleCN: 设想一个无人应答的假想情形。

items.meaning: in an assumed or imagined situation
items.meaningCN: 在假设或假想的情况下（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Hypothetically, the plan could work if costs fell.
items.exampleCN: 假定成本下降，这个计划理论上可行。

items.meaningCN: 提出假说（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Researchers hypothesize that the sound guides the fish home.
items.exampleCN: 研究者假设这种声音能引导鱼回到出生地。

items.meaning: under the skin, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 皮下的（如皮下注射；hypo- 在下 + derma 皮肤）
items.example: The nurse prepared a hypodermic needle.
items.exampleCN: 护士准备好了一支皮下注射针。

items.meaning: a body temperature dangerously below normal
items.meaningCN: 低体温；体温过低（hypo- 在下 + therme 热）
items.example: The climbers were treated for hypothermia.
items.exampleCN: 登山者接受了低体温治疗。

items.meaning: a proposition to be defended; a long research essay
items.meaningCN: 待辩护的命题；长篇研究论文（希腊语“放置、命题”）
items.example: Her thesis argues that the two reforms were one process.
items.exampleCN: 她的论文主张这两场改革其实是一个过程。

items.meaning: the direct opposite of a proposition
items.meaningCN: 对立命题；正相反的说法（anti- 反对 + thesis 放置）
items.example: His calm manner is the antithesis of her urgency.
items.exampleCN: 他的从容正是她那种急切的对照。

items.meaning: a putting together of parts into a whole
items.meaningCN: 综合；合成（syn- 一起 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The book is a synthesis of history and economics.
items.exampleCN: 这本书是历史学与经济学的综合。

items.meaning: a phrase placed beside the main sentence; a bracket
items.meaningCN: 插入语；圆括号（para- 旁 + en- 内 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The date appears in parentheses at the end.
items.exampleCN: 日期放在末尾的圆括号里。

latinEntries.meaning: base, groundwork; basis of an argument
latinEntries.meaningCN: 地基、基础；论证的依据（晚期拉丁语原样借入）

latinEntries.structure: Greek thesis, from PIE *dhe- 'to set, put'

latinEntries.meaning: a putting under; assumption, used to translate Greek hypothesis
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放在下面；假定（中世纪拉丁语用来翻译希腊语 hypothesis）
